detail.desc: at the obama foundation, our mission is to inspire, empower, and connect people to change their world. we seek to build an active democratic culture where people are equipped and motivated to make change in the communities where they live, work, and play. right here on the south side of chicago, we’re building a home for this vision, a global center for change with a range of opportunities - coordinated programming, community outreach events, educational moments, and more - that invite visitors from down the block or across the globe to turn hope into action.achieving our ambitious goals starts with an exceptional team built on our hope to action values - courage, empathy, integrity, accountability, community, inclusivity, pragmatism, resilience, imagination, and hope. a framework that anyone, anywhere, can use to build trust, activate participation, and expand opportunity in their community.purpose of the rolethe press secretary will play a pivotal role in pitching the obama foundation’s stories with external audiences, with a focus on traditional legacy media but also a lens toward creator/influencer cultivation in partnership with the editorial team. the role will focus on audience cultivation, prioritizing earned media with a lens toward supporting and enhancing the foundation’s strategic communications efforts.the press secretary will be responsible for surfacing stories and pitching external outlets, managing public relations, launching special projects and working with external pr resources and consultants. additionally, this role will drive program launches and major events for the communications team and provide strategic leadership and management within the communications function. this role encompasses working across the foundation, on all initiatives and programming, ensuring cohesive and impactful messaging and traditional and new media outreach.as the press secretary, you’ll be reporting directly to the vice president of communications.core job responsibilitiesstrategic communications & media relationssupport the vp of communications in developing and executing a public relations strategy that translates the foundation’s mission to key external stakeholders.cultivate and maintain relationships with national and local traditional media, securing high-impact earned media coverage.work with the social media team to engage audience-based communicators, such as influencers, to amplify the foundation’s messaging.storytelling & message developmentsurface, package, and pitch compelling stories that highlight the foundation’s impact, leadership, and programming.ensure messaging consistency and alignment across all public-facing communications.major events & program launcheslead media strategy, planning, and execution for major foundation events, announcements, and program milestones.collaborate with internal teams and external partners to maximize press coverage and public engagement.crisis communications & rapid responsesupport the development of crisis communications protocols and playbooks.provide strategic counsel and rapid response to emerging media opportunities and challenges.external partnerships & consultant managementmanage relationships with external pr agencies, consultants, and strategic communications partners.oversee contract deliverables to ensure alignment with the foundation’s communications goals.team leadership & cross-functional collaborationprovide mentorship and leadership within the communications team, fostering a collaborative and high-performing work environment.work cross-functionally across departments to ensure cohesive messaging and media strategy.special projects & emerging opportunitieslead and oversee special communications projects that advance the foundation’s mission and visibility.identify and execute new opportunities for audience engagement through media and strategic partnerships.required qualifications8 years in public relations, media relations, or strategic communications, preferably in a nonprofit, government, or mission-driven organization.established network of national and local press contacts, with a proven track record of securing high-impact coverage.strong ability to identify and package compelling narratives that align with institutional goals.experience navigating media crises and rapid response scenarios.experience managing teams, external consultants, and cross-functional projects.ability to operate in a fast-paced environment with strategic agility and discretion.the salary range for this role is between $104,310 and $130,435.this is a hybrid role based at the obama presidential center.for an overview of our benefits package, including insurance, detail.desc: job description:role purpose & overviewthe sr. director strategic business communications – digital technologies is the dedicated communications advisor to a mars snacking leadership team (mslt) member and the snacking dt leadership team. embedded in the business, the role connects strategic internal communications, executive visibility, and reputation to support business goals and growth.the partner brings strong transformation fluency—connecting strategy, change, and communications so priority programs are understood, embraced, and translated into new capabilities and ways of working.principal duties & responsibilitiesstrategic counsel & communicationsserve as a senior business partner to the cdio and snacking dt leadership team, helping shape digital strategy and business decisions from the start. advise on priorities, timing, and what decisions mean for stakeholders, communications, and reputation.develop the communications and engagement strategy that embeds the digital strategy across the company’s transformation and integration work. connect dt workstreams and help senior sponsors agree on a shared story, how the work fits together, and the outcomes to achieve—turning strategy into leadership commitments, associate behaviors, and ways of working across functions and markets.partner with dt leaders and cross-functional teams to engage associates around business objectives, growth priorities, and results. shape the approach to key internal and external moments, choosing the right channels, timing, and stories.make complex digital priorities clear through compelling content and real examples that show progress and impact, bring functions and markets together, and connect segment goals with the enterprise digital strategy.executive & leadership visibilitydefine the executive positioning and leadership engagement strategy for the cdio, connecting the strategy with dt’s business, transformation, and integration priorities; establish the leadership narrative, stakeholder priorities, and desired outcomes that guide reputation building efforts.shape the long-term thought leadership agenda with the cdio, using business priorities, stakeholder insights, and digital trends to choose where mars snacking should lead the conversation on technology, data and analytics, and ai.develop content and materials to support primarily the cdio on leadership engagement, including town halls, leadership meetings, leader messages, q&a, video scripts, presentations, and intranet articles; equip next-level leaders with aligned materials.support executive readiness and presence through messaging development, panel preparation, and leadership briefing materials.partner with external communications on media relations and issues management, connecting executive visibility to business and reputation goals.transformation & change enablementin partnership with the transformation communications team, lead priority digital transformation programs, building understanding, readiness, and commitment to new capabilities and ways of working.embed communications in transformation and change plans from the outset, aligned to business impacts, milestones, and audience needs.equip leaders and markets with narratives, tools, and feedback loops that address barriers, reinforce accountability, and accelerate adoption.measurement & continuous improvementset communications objectives tied to digital priorities, measuring understanding, engagement, leadership effectiveness, readiness, and adoption.combine analytics, feedback, and business signals to identify gaps and continuously improve strategy, content, and channel performance.prioritize and manage agency, creative, multimedia, and freelance support against the highest-value outcomes.context & scopeto fulfill the requirements of this role, you will work closely with senior leaders and cross-functional colleagues across dt, integration and corporate affairs. you’ll operate as a trusted advisor within a diverse, global communications community—balancing strategic counsel with hands-on execution in a complex, matrixed environment.what we are looking forexperience: bachelor’s degree required (communications, public affairs, journalism, or related field preferred), 12+ years of experience in communications, corporate affairs, or related roles.executive counsel: demonstrated success advising c-suite and senior leaders, influencing decisions, and providing constructive challenge.digital transformation acumen: fluency in digital strategy, ai, data and analytics, technology modernization, and enterprise transformation, with the ability to connect technical change to business value.storytelling & delivery: exceptional writing, presentation, and project leadership skills across executive, digital, social, and live channels in a global environment.what can you expect from mars? work with diverse and talented associates, all guided by the five principles. join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today. a strong focus on learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house mars university. an industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.the base pay range for this position at commencement of employment is between the range listed below, however, base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. the total compensation package for this position will include variable pay, medical and dental benefits, participation in 401k plan, and paid time off benefits. details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an applicant receives an offer of employment.the pay range shown is applicable to all us locations listed within the job posting:usd 192,560.00 - usd 264,770.00

detail.desc: littelfuse (nasdaq: lfus) is a diversified industrial technology manufacturing company shaping solutions for the safe and efficient transfer of electrical energy. headquartered in chicago, illinois, usa, we serve customers across industrial, transportation, and electronics markets worldwide. with approximately 16,000 employees we design and manufacture innovative technologies that support electrification, energy efficiency, and advanced automation. our global reach is matched by a culture that empowers innovation and long-term growth. guided by our principles we care, we succeed with our customers, and we own the outcome, we work collaboratively, think boldly, and deliver solutions that move industries forward.role summarydrive system-level adoption across industrial oems, automation machinery builders, commercial hvac manufacturers, and advanced electromechanical systems. develop integrated protection and sensing solutions and partner with engineering teams to influence architecture decisions for motors, drives, controls, thermal systems, and embedded electronics.key responsibilitiessystem solution development: build reference solutions for hvac equipment, industrial machinery, commercial refrigeration, automation equipment, and control panels using littelfuse protection, sensing, relays, and semiconductors.design collaboration: engage oem r&d and system architects early in the lifecycle to shape specs, improve reliability, and coordinate protection/thermal performance.segment marketing & positioning: own messaging and campaigns for industrial oem & hvac; tailor by sub-segment (motors/drives, compressors, controls, embedded electronics).sales & channel enablement: provide design tools, overcurrent/thermal coordination guides, fault-tree demos, and application notes that speed qualification and certification.thought leadership: produce best-practice content on motor protection, lv control circuit reliability, inverter-driven hvac protection, and sensor-enabled safety.market intelligence: track regulatory/efficiency trends, competitive offerings, and technology shifts in industrial automation and hvac.qualificationseducation (required): bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechatronics, or mechanical engineering with controls/ee emphasis.experience: 7+ years in industrial oem, hvac systems, industrial automation, or electromechanical system design; proven record of influencing specs and securing design-ins.technical expertise: motor control, variable-speed drives, sensor integration, circuit protection, power semiconductors, emc/surge, and system reliability engineering.communication: strong technical writing and presentations for engineering and procurement stakeholders.attributes: customer-facing, hands-on problem solver, collaborative across product, applications, sales, and channel teams.success metricsincrease in qualified design-ins and design wins in industrial oem & hvac accounts.incremental revenue and pipeline attributable to system solutions and enablement assets.expanded multi-product adoption per oem and improved voc satisfaction.travelup to 30% - for customer visits, piloting, and industry events.artificial intelligence (ai) tools may be used in some portions of the candidate review process for this position, however, all final employment decisions will be made by a person.salary range$104,400 - $161,760the salary offered will vary depending on your location, job-related skills, knowledge, and experience.at littelfuse, we support employee growth and development. guided by our culture principles, our teams work together to deliver value for customers and make a positive impact in the communities where we operate. we are an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone has the opportunity to grow and contribute. we offer competitive compensation and benefits, performance-based incentives, flexible work arrangements, and development opportunities.

intelligence, cultural signals, category context, competitive activity, and channel behavior to identify meaningful patterns. develop actionable insights and confidently present them to clients and internal teams. originate insights that improve creative relevance, campaign effectiveness, customer experience, or business value. distinguish observations from insights and connect findings to a clear implication for strategy, creative, media, or measurement. turn complex or unstructured inputs into clear, compelling, and error-free client deliverables. lead the development of creative briefs, performance narratives, content and messaging frameworks, audience and journey strategies, testing roadmaps, and optimization recommendations. tell a persuasive story with data, making the strategic implication and recommended action easy to understand. ensure creative strategy reflects audience needs, channel context, journey stage, brand considerations, and measurable business goals. performance creative strategy. support the development of junior strategists through clear feedback, knowledge sharing, and collaborative working practices. qualifications4+ years of professional detail.desc: brown distributing company is a leading beverage distributor throughout the state of virginia. since 1919, brown distributing has grown into a beverage distribution business with combined sales of over 3 million cases annually and serving in excess of 3,000 retailers with nearly 200 employees. brown distributing offers their employees competitive compensation, complete benefit package, including medical, dental, vision, company paid life insurance and a 401k employer match.the strategic brand & marketing manager will lead the strategy, development, and day-to-day execution of the richmond coffee ready to-drink “rtd” coffee brand within the richmond market, along with future brands and markets as the portfolio grows. this is a hands-on, roll-up-your sleeves role that owns the brand from concept to shelf: managing co-packer relationships, directing brand and packaging design, building marketing programs, and ensuring a strong supplier experience. this role partners closely with the sales team and with chain, independent, and on-premise retail accounts to build brand awareness, grow distribution, open new accounts, and deliver volume and profitability goals. this role will also identify and lead brand expansion opportunities that drive future growth, and will manage the sampling & events coordinator and the brand’s in-market sampling program.compensation$85,000-$110,000/yearvehicle allowance: $825/monthphone allowance: $75/monthschedulefull time position to include nights and weekends, and travel as needed to co-packers, suppliers, markets, and events.essential duties & responsibilities: include the following. other duties may be assigned.brand strategy & portfolio management: own the brand strategy, positioning, and annual brand plans for richmond coffee and additional brands as the portfolio expands, including the brand calendar, pricing strategy, sku mix, case volume and sales goals, and brand p&l oversight.co-packer management: source, onboard, and manage co-packer relationships, including production scheduling, run minimums, quality standards, cost negotiations, and contract compliance.product development: lead new product and line-extension development from concept through commercialization, including consumer and category research, flavor development, formulation, shelf-life testing, packaging, and launch timing.innovation pipeline & sku management: build and manage a multi year innovation pipeline; evaluate sku performance and recommend additions, line extensions, and sku rationalization based on velocity and profitability.brand & packaging design: direct brand identity, packaging, and point of-sale design with internal resources and outside artists, ensuring a consistent look, voice, and message across every touchpoint.brand guidelines & sales tools: create and maintain brand guidelines, sell sheets, price sheets, and digital assets; develop point-of-sale (pos/posm) and merchandising materials and ensure the sales team and retail accounts execute the brand consistently in market; develop display, cooler and cold-vault placement, shelf, and secondary-placement programs that turn awareness into purchase, and audit in-market execution during store visits.supplier experience: manage relationships with ingredient, packaging, and materials co-packers to ensure quality, on-time delivery, and cost efficiency; resolve supply issues quickly and build long-term partnerships.marketing programs: develop and execute integrated, 360-degree marketing plans, including digital and social media, influencer and consumer engagement, retail and chain promotions, trade marketing, pr, local community and cause-marketing programs, and partnerships, to build awareness and drive trial and repeat purchase. build richmond coffee’s identity as a local, community-rooted brand through partnerships with richmond-area organizations including non-profit, colleges and universities, sports and entertainment venues, festivals, and local businesses.sampling & events oversight: set the strategy, budget, and goals for sampling and event programs; build an annual sampling and events calendar that targets high-traffic retail accounts, priority prospect accounts, chain in-store demos, and community events; set measurable goals for every activation (samples distributed, consumer engagements, sales lift, and new placements); ensure each sampling event is coordinated with the sales team so it converts into orders, displays, or new accounts; direct the sampling & events coordinator and review post-event reporting and roi, reallocating sampling dollars to the activations that drive the most sales.brand expansion & future growth: identify and evaluate new markets, channels, products, and brand opportunities; build business cases and lead go-to-market planning for expansion.sales team partnership: partner with the sales team to develop sell-in presentations, quarterly programming, and sales incentives; support chain, independent, and on-premise account objectives; and conduct market visits and ride-withs with sales representatives to drive distribution, placements, displays, new accounts, and velocity.pricing & market planning: support pricing, retailer margin structures, and planning for new markets and channels in partnership with sales leadership.market & consumer insights: monitor category trends, competitive activity, and consumer insights using syndicated scan data (such as nielsen, circana/iri), internal sales and depletion reporting, consumer feedback captured at sampling events, and consumer research to guide brand decisions and identify new opportunities.budget & performance reporting: manage the brand marketing, sampling, and trade spend budgets; track key metrics (depletions, distribution points, velocity, share, new accounts opened, samples distributed, sampling-to-sale conversion, social media reach and engagement, and roi); and report results, post-program analysis, and recommendations to leadership.industry presence: represent the brand at sales meetings, retailer meetings and reviews, trade shows, and community events, serving as the brand ambassador internally and externally.regulatory & labeling compliance: work with co-packers and suppliers to ensure labeling, claims, and packaging meet applicable fda and regulatory requirements; ensure sampling programs follow food-safety, product-handling, and retailer and venue sampling requirements.new account development: partner with the sales team to identify, prioritize, and pursue new accounts across grocery, convenience, drug, on-premise, foodservice, office, hospitality, and college and university channels; use sampling and in-store demos as a door-opener with buyers and store managers; track new accounts opened, distribution points gained, and reorder rates.brand ambassador program & sampling standards: with the sampling & events coordinator, build and maintain a team of trained part time brand ambassadors (recruiting, training, product knowledge, talking points, and scheduling); set sampling execution standards covering setup and presentation, product handling and food safety, cold-chain, sample inventory accountability, and photo and recap reporting.digital & social media: own the brand’s social media channels and content calendar; capture content from sampling events, accounts, and the community; grow followers and engagement; and use geo-targeted digital, local influencers, and user-generated content to drive consumers to retail locations where the brand is sold.supervisory responsibilitiesdirectly supervises the sampling & events coordinator, and direct the work of outside artists, designers, and vendors. carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization’s policies and applicable laws. responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; and addressing complaints and resolving problems.qualificationsbachelor’s degree in marketing, business, or a related field (or an equivalent combination of education and experience), and at least 5 years of brand management or marketing experience in the beverage (alcohol or non-alcohol) or consumer packaged goods industry. hands-on experience managing vendors; co-packers or contract manufacturers, leading packaging and brand design projects, and launching new products a plus. beverage distributor experience, rtd coffee or beverage experience, experience building and running sampling, demo, or brand ambassador programs, established relationships with richmond-area retailers and community organizations, and prior supervisory experience are preferred. working knowledge of beverage distribution, including chain account programming and resets, depletion reporting, pricing, and trade spend management. experience using syndicated scan data and internal sales reporting to build fact-based selling stories. proficiency in microsoft office; social media management and content tools, and sales/depletion data platforms is a plus. all final applicants will be required to comply and pass all drug, background, and driving checks

in the us market.candidates with experience in both brick-and-mortar retail and e-commerce will be preferred.key objectiveto strengthen the company's brand presence in the us market by developing effective brand strategies, driving consumer engagement, enhancing brand visibility, and supporting long-term business growth

job title: director of communications reports to: vice president of communications  location: lincoln, ne (hybrid)  status: full-time  position overview  the nebraska hospital association (nha) is seeking a versatile and detail-oriented director of communications to join our fast-paced team. this role is perfect for someone who can take complicated issues and turn them into clear, compelling communications that inform, engage, and build excitement. we are looking for someone who is organized, curious, creative, flexible, and comfortable managing multiple priorities. this position reports directly to the vice president of communications and works across departments to ensure the nha’s voice is clear, consistent, and impactful.  key responsibilities  core content production developing and producing high-quality content supporting nha’s core functions, including advocacy, member engagement, education, workforce initiatives, public affairs, and major association programs and events. copywriting to draft compelling content for newsletters and other written content. translate complex health care, policy, and association issues into clear, accessible messaging for a variety of audiences. utilize basic design tools (e.g., canva, adobe) to create professional digital assets.  coordination of website updates to maintain an accurate and professional digital presence.  serve as a final line of defense for quality control, ensuring all nha communications are polished, professional, accurate, and follow nha brand guidelines.  event content and messaging help lead the strategy, content development, and outreach for nha’s signature programs, webinars, and conferences.  ensure our events match nha’s organizational values, goals, and objectives. design interactive q&as, live polling, and feedback mechanisms. build excitement leading up to events and extend engagement afterward through recaps, highlights, and follow-up communications. internal communications manage the flow of information inside the company to keep employees informed, aligned, and engaged. communicate organizational news, priorities, and important updates through email, newsletters, staff meetings, and other internal channels. translate organizational goals and priorities into clear messaging that helps employees understand nha’s direction and how their work contributes.  help strengthen organizational culture, connect daily work to organizational values, and guide teams through shifts or new policies. qualifications  bachelor’s degree preferred.  strong attention to detail and highly organized.  proficiency in microsoft suite, email marketing software, social media management tools, and basic graphic design.  a curious mind and a strong work ethic. brings fresh ideas, asks "why," and continually looks for ways to improve how we communicate and engage. about us:  the nebraska hospital association (nha) is a statewide trade association representing nebraska's hospitals and health systems since 1927.     the hospital and health system field is the only sector of nebraska’s economy that touches every citizen and business of nebraska. not only do hospitals support a healthy nebraska and provide essential health care services, they are also among the largest employers and economic drivers in most regions of the state. hospitals and health care are the foundation upon which communities in nebraska are built.     the nha serves as the influential voice of its members in the health care legislative and public arenas, promoting delivery of quality health care and influencing public opinion of hospitals and health networks. members depend on the association for information, advice, education and changes in health care regulations, legislation, trends and other issues.     hospitals are the stewards of good health. through our partnerships with representatives in the health care industry, legislators, government and citizens, the nha is able to assist in the development of strong, healthy communities.  mission  to serve nebraska hospitals by being the most trusted voice and influential advocate in health care and a driver of hospital quality and safety improvement.  vision  to improve the health and well-being of all nebraskans by supporting and unifying nebraska hospitals.  benefits:  by joining the nebraska hospital association, you become one of a spirited and dynamic team that is driven to succeed.  the nha offers an outstanding salary and benefits package that includes health, dental and vision insurance; life insurance, long-term and short-term disability; vacation, sick/personal leave and paid holidays; health savings account; and a 401(k) salary deferral plan with employer match and contributions as well as a profit-sharing plan. in addition, the position receives a fitness center reimbursement, educational assistance for continuing education and membership dues as budgeted in professional organizations or societies.  salary:  commensurate with experience.  physical requirements:  walking, standing, and sitting for prolonged periods.  must have or obtain a valid driver’s license in the state of nebraska.  working conditions:  hybrid. the position requires 2-3 days in the office in addition to occasional travel to meetings and association events and may require time away from home outside normal working hours.  at the nebraska hospital association, our mission is to improve the health and well-being of all nebraskans. we believe that a diverse, inclusive team is essential to achieving that vision. the nha is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences.reasonable accommodations: the nha is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our application and hiring process. if you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact andy hale at ahale@nebraskahospitals.org position reports to:   vice president of communications  position classification:  flsa: exempt  please note: this job description is not detail.desc: reports to: stakeholder engagement and communications program manager, rhtplocation: charleston, west virginia (on site)position type: full-time, exempt (at-will)position overview: the communications specialist will serve as the voice of the west virginia rural health transformation program (rhtp), translating complex healthcare metrics, state policies, and programmatic updates into powerful public narratives. managing public messaging for a historic initiative funded at $200 million or more under governor patrick morrisey’s vision, this professional role ensures transparent, consistent, and engaging communications across all state stakeholders, media outlets, and local communities. reporting directly to the stakeholder engagement and communications program manager, this position demands a highly creative, fast-moving, and detail-oriented producer who takes ownership of projects from concept to completion. the specialist will turn raw ideas into polished, high-quality visual and written assets that support broad public input campaigns and direct partner feedback loops. the position ensures that the rhtp remains a community-driven initiative designed to improve health outcomes and workforce participation across west virginia.key responsibilitiescreative content & graphic design: own the end-to-end design, layout, and production of high-quality digital and print collateral—including infographics, toolkits, social media graphics, presentation decks, and multi-media components—ensuring all deliverables are publication-ready.high-impact writing & copyediting: author compelling, plain-language written content that distills dense health data, medical logistics, and project milestones into accessible copy for newsletters, press releases, website landing pages, and executive program summaries.programmatic publicity & campaigns: create tailored promotional, educational, and public-facing collateral to support public awareness, continuous feedback loops, and targeted community input sessions for rhtp's seven core flagship initiatives.managerial & multi-agency coordination: proactively assist the program manager in preparing rapid-turnaround briefing materials and project reports. efficiently route drafts through required multi-tiered approval workflows, incorporating feedback seamlessly from state agency partners.media & digital presence strategy: manage program channels, track digital audience engagement metrics, draft formal media advisories, and foster collaborative relationships with regional and state journalists.crisis & public advisory support: track public inquiries, monitor perception trends across the state, and advise senior leadership on timely, factual messaging adjustments to maintain programmatic transparency.core competenciesexceptional writing & visual execution: advanced capacity to quickly transform rough concepts into beautifully designed, impeccably written, and clear public communications.ownership & autonomy: a fast-paced, self-starting mindset with precise attention to detail and a commitment to executing multi-platform deliverables with minimal supervision.strategic storytelling: proven ability to synthesize dense health analytics or complex federal regulations into narrative forms that build community trust and engagement.interagency diplomacy: capacity to handle feedback smoothly across internal rhtp teams, state departments, and external oversight partners while maintaining strict operational deadlines.minimum qualificationseducation: a bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, marketing, or a related field is required; a master’s degree is preferred.experience: 3–5 years of professional communications, public relations, or media management experience is required. direct exposure to large-scale public health public relations, government communications, or healthcare marketing campaigns is preferred.technical proficiencies: proven portfolio demonstrating advanced capability in visual design tools (such as adobe creative suite, canva, or similar software) and email marketing engines/content management systems.compensation & benefitscompensation: commensurate with qualifications.health & wellness: comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance plans.work-life balance: generous paid leave accrual (vacation and sick time) alongside paid state holidays.limited‑term notice: this position is a full-time, term-limited appointment for a period of up to four (4) years and career-defining. vinci is at that moment.we're tackling one of the biggest challenges in technology: the growing gap between the complexity of the hardware the world needs and our ability to understand how it will actually work before it's built. as ai accelerates demand for more powerful chips and increasingly sophisticated electronic systems, traditional engineering tools are struggling to keep pace. it's one of the defining challenges of the ai era—and vinci has a breakthrough solution that's already generating coverage in the technology and business press, along with engagement with leading journalists and podcasters.we've pioneered the physics intelligence platform, bringing ai-native physics computation to hardware engineering. instead of waiting days or weeks for answers, engineers can understand the physical consequences of their designs in seconds to minutes, explore vastly more alternatives, and discover better solutions. this isn't another incremental improvement to engineering software. it's a new computational capability with the potential to transform how the world's most advanced hardware is designed.and this isn't just a vision. vinci's technology has been adopted across more than 40 engineering programs at some of the world's leading semiconductor and electronics companies. we've just raised a $250 million series b at a $1.5 billion valuation, physics intelligence. to make vinci a company journalists want to cover, podcasters want to interview, industry leaders want to engage with, and engineers want to follow. we want to move faster, loot labs is on a mission to make collecting fun. we believe that every collectible tells a story: of passion, nostalgia, and discovery.through our flagship product, boxed.gg we are reimagining how the world collects by blending digital entertainment with tangible rewards, delivering nostalgia and discovery straight to the fans' doorsteps.we are...community first: we've served 1m collectors and foster an active community of over 145k+ discord members. ambitiously led: led by veterans from microsoft, twitch, 2k, and boeing. remote-first: we value high autonomy, low ego, and trust our team to build from anywhere in the world. since our inception in 2023, we’ve seen significant year-over-year growth. and now we're gearing up for our most ambitious year yet, with major expansions planned across product offerings, strategic partnerships, and next-generation collector experiences. if you’re ready to build products that spark joy at a global scale, you’re in the right place.role descriptionreporting to the content lead, the social media manager owns boxed's social channels and turns attention from collectors into new users. your job is to make boxed the account the hobby actually follows: fast, native to collector culture, on-trend, and unmistakably ours.reach matters, but it isn't the scoreboard. social is an acquisition channel for us, and your work should show up in signups, app installs, and first purchases. you'll write, shoot, edit, and post yourself, and build the systems, partners, and creator sources that let output scale beyond what one person can make.in your first year, success means social is a measurable acquisition channel: signups, installs, and first purchases attributed to owned social every month and growing quarter over quarter, a real hobby audience across both tcg and sports, and a steady pipeline of proven formats feeding paid creative.key responsibilitieschannel strategy - own day-to-day strategy, publishing, and performance across tiktok, youtube (including shorts), instagram, x, and reddit, with a distinct playbook for each. trend spotting - catch trends, sounds, memes, and hobby moments early, and get on-brand content live the same day while they're still rising. content creation - write, shoot, and edit native short-form content, and develop recurring series such as pack openings, pull reactions, hobby explainers, and community spotlights. user acquisition - drive signups, app installs, first purchases, and referral activity from social, and test calls to action and conversion paths from content to product. measurement - work with growth and analytics on attribution (utms, link-in-bio, promo codes, app deep links) and report acquisition by channel, not just reach. sports audience - grow the sports card audience with the same intent as tcg. team collaboration - partner with influencer, field, and community teams to amplify creator content, turn cons and nationals into a month of posts, and promote the referral program and discord. qualificationsexperience: 3+ years running social for a consumer brand, app, or media company, with a track record of growing an audience and tying it to signups, installs, or revenue. editorial / content background: experience as a creator, editor, writer, or producer at a media brand, publisher, or creator-led company. you can write a hook and tell a story in 15 seconds. collectibles knowledge: working fluency in trading cards and collectibles, whether tcg (pokémon, magic, one piece, lorcana) or sports cards. you know what a chase card is, why grading matters, and what makes a pull go viral. trend awareness: you live on tiktok, youtube, x, and reddit, and know how to adapt a trend so it feels native to the brand rather than forced. technical skills: comfortable shooting on a phone and editing in capcut, premiere, or similar, and fluent in native platform analytics. communication skills: sharp writing and a consistent brand voice across every post. preferred skillsactive collector: you collect, break, or grade cards yourself and know the hobby's creators and communities. creator experience: you've built a following of your own on any platform. paid social exposure: experience feeding organic content into paid teams or working with ugc creators. app growth: experience driving installs for a mobile app. speed and volume: you ship a lot, learn fast, and keep quality high while doing it. adaptability: comfortable working in a fast-paced, remote environment with shifting priorities. company benefits:15 days of accrued pto7 days of sick-leave, front-loaded at the start of the year10 paid company holidaysgenerous vision, dental, and health benefits, with 97% contribution to premium401k matching

foundation.assess market context: work with canada and un leads to assess the political economy, institutional mandates, priorities, capabilities, and constraints shaping each market, including advance foundation priorities and the expected impact of its contributions. develop market-specific policy proposals, arguments, and concrete asks with relevant foundation teams, supporting market leads in developing their advocacy approaches.support broader policy and development architecture work: partner with the deputy director on broader policy and development architecture questions, i.e. teams to ensure work remains aligned with agreed objectives.your experience10+ years of experience in advocacy, government relations, public policy, multilateral engagement, or strategy, ideally in a strategic direction while developing and executing flexible, practical implementation plans.experience engaging external partners and managing contracts, including scopes of work, budgets, timelines, and deliverables.excellent verbal and written communication skills, with an ability to synthesize complex concepts, evidence, political context, and recommendations succinctly and persuasively.demonstrated ability to lead ambiguous or emerging workstreams, assess competing priorities, and deliver high-quality analysis and products for multiple internal collaborators.knowledge submission or other immigration support from the company (eg: h-1b, o-1, l-1, e, opt, stem-opt, cpt, tn, j-1, etc.).the salary range for this role is $212,800 to $329,800 usd. we recognize high-wage support this diversity through all our employment practices.all applicants and employees who are drawn to serve our mission will enjoy equality of opportunity and fair treatment without regard to strategies that improve time-to-therapy, patient initiation, treatment persistence, and access expansion. evaluate payer trends, reimbursement barriers, medicaid opportunities, and competitive access changes to inform brand strategy. omnichannel & data-driven marketing lead omnichannel strategy and optimization across all customer segments. establish kpis and performance dashboards to monitor january 2027salary: $80,000 - $90,000youth crossroads, founded in 1974, supports youth, guiding them through life’s challenges, and inspiring them to discover new opportunities for personal development, healthy relationships, and positive community involvement. we seek to provide youth with a comprehensive system of support, positive structures, and role models to help them navigate the readiness, and community service. all yc services are provided with a culturally affirming and trauma-informed approach.position summarythe director of external affairs is responsible for strengthening youth crossroads’ external relationships, advancing its fundraising efforts, and elevating the organization’s visibility and community presence. working in partnership with the executive director, board of directors, and internal leadership, the director will develop and execute strategies that cultivate philanthropic support, deepen corporate and community partnerships, and communicate the organization’s impact.this role will focus on building sustainable donor relationships, expanding contributed revenue, strengthening external engagement, and aligning fundraising leadership and board members to advance fundraising and external engagement goals.key responsibilities1. executive partnership and strategic alignment● partner with the executive director and active pipeline of prospective supporters.● identify opportunities to expand corporate partnerships and sponsorships that align with youth crossroads’ mission and funding priorities.● support annual giving campaigns and targeted fundraising initiatives designed to strengthen donor engagement and contributed revenue.● monitor fundraising performance, maintain accurate revenue projections, and practices.3. external relations and community engagement● serve as a visible ambassador for youth crossroads within the philanthropic, corporate, civic, and community sectors.● build and maintain relationships with community leaders, businesses, foundations, civic organizations, and other stakeholders across berwyn, cicero, and surrounding communities.● represent the organization at selected networking events, community gatherings, speaking engagements, and donor cultivation opportunities.● identify and pursue strategic partnerships that expand organizational visibility, strengthen community relationships, and support mission-aligned opportunities.● collaborate with program and organizational leaders to identify opportunities for external engagement that demonstrate the impact of youth crossroads’ work.4. communications and organizational visibility● collaborate with internal staff and leadership to ensure consistent, compelling communication of youth crossroads’ mission, development of donor-facing materials, presentations, organizational updates, and partnership proposals.● identify opportunities to elevate organizational visibility through strategic partnerships, community engagement, and relevant external platforms.5. board engagement and accountability● partner with the executive director to engage board members in donor cultivation, relationship-building, and fundraising activities.● provide board and leadership updates on donor pipeline development, fundraising performance, partnership activity, and progress toward established goals.● establish measurable annual objectives and participate in periodic performance reviews to assess progress and identify opportunities for improvement.● participate in organizational meetings, professional development, and required training.qualifications● bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or relevant professional certification preferred.● five to seven years of progressive experience in relationships.● demonstrated initiative, proactive in identifying what needs to be done and taking ownership to move work forward.● experience supporting fundraising initiatives, donor stewardship, and revenue development.● strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to represent an organization effectively to external audiences.● experience collaborating with executive leadership and supporting board engagement in organizational priorities.● ability to develop and execute strategies, manage multiple priorities, and use data to monitor detail.desc: company description:rafiki coalition for health and wellness is a san francisco-based nonprofit dedicated to eliminating health inequities and improving the lives of black, african american, and marginalized communities in the bay area. for over 35 years, we have provided a safe, welcoming space where health, healing, and hope come together. we offer a holistic range of services, including free and low-cost health screenings, hiv prevention and care, mental health counseling, housing and economic support, fitness classes, and nutrition programs. guided by a belief that wellness is more than the absence of illness, we embrace a whole-person approach that honors the cultural, social, and emotional needs of our community.at rafiki, we are more than a service provider. we are a trusted partner, advocate, and resource. our work is rooted in compassion, cultural humility, and a commitment to social justice. every day, our team stands with our community to communities, rafiki coalition is the place to make a meaningful impactjob description:under the direction of the director of development and communications, the communications manager leads rafiki coalition's internal and external communications. the position develops clear, consistent messaging; manages digital and print communications; supports media and community outreach; and increases awareness of rafiki's mission, programs, services, and impact. the communications manager also supports development activities through fundraising communications, donor materials, sponsorship promotion, and funder-facing content. the position may supervise staff, contractors, interns, or volunteers assigned to communications projects. responsibilities communications strategy and brand management develop and implement annual communications and marketing plans aligned with organizational priorities and approved by the executive director. maintain consistent messaging, voice, visual identity, and use of the rafiki coalition brand across departments, programs, campaigns, and public materials. create communications calendars, establish priorities and deadlines, and coordinate information from staff and program leaders. monitor communications results and provide practical reports and recommendations to the executive director. content and publications write, edit, and coordinate print and electronic materials, including newsletters, brochures, fact sheets, presentations, flyers, organizational updates, and the annual report. translate program information, community needs, and organizational results into accurate, accessible, and culturally responsive content for varied audiences. manage the review and approval process for public-facing materials and maintain organized communications files, templates, photographs, and content resources. coordinate designers, printers, photographers, videographers, and other vendors as needed. digital communications manage website content and coordinate website maintenance to keep information accurate, current, accessible, and easy to use. plan, create, schedule, and monitor social media and email communications in support of programs, events, community education, and organizational priorities. maintain digital content standards and use basic analytics to assess reach, engagement, and opportunities for improvement. coordinate timely communications during urgent, sensitive, or rapidly changing situations, in consultation with the executive director and appropriate leaders. media community and partner relations develop media outreach materials, including press releases, media advisories, background information, talking points, opinion pieces, and responses to media inquiries. build and maintain working relationships with media, community partners, coalitions, issue experts, and organizations serving rafiki's communities. support public events, campaigns, and community engagement activities through messaging, promotion, materials, and communications logistics. prepare the executive director and other designated representatives for interviews, presentations, public statements, and community appearances. development support partner with the executive director, development staff, and consultants to create fundraising appeals, donor communications, sponsorship materials, campaign content, and event promotion. contribute communications content for grant proposals, funder reports, acknowledgments, impact stories, and other development materials. help communicate the results of funded programs accurately and consistently while meeting applicable funder recognition requirements. support donor and sponsor cultivation through coordinated messaging and appropriate communications follow-up. planning administration and supervision develop and monitor the communications budget; manage vendors, contracts, schedules, and project deliverables within approved authority. coordinate multiple projects, clarify roles and approvals, and keep the executive director informed of progress, risks, deadlines, and decisions needed. supervise and train assigned staff, contractors, interns, or volunteers and provide clear expectations and feedback. follow organizational policies and protect confidential, sensitive, and personally identifiable information in all communications. perform other duties as assigned.requirements:bachelor's degree in communications, marketing, journalism, public relations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. at least five years of progressively responsible experience in communications, marketing, public relations, or related work, preferably in a nonprofit or community-based organization. strong writing, editing, verbal communication, interpersonal, and project management skills, with careful attention to accuracy and detail. experience managing websites, email communications, social media, publications, media relations, and communications vendors or consultants. ability to communicate effectively with diverse communities and represent rafiki's mission and work in a culturally responsive manner. working knowledge of microsoft office and common content management, email marketing, social media, design, and analytics tools. additional information:this is a full time positionhybrid flsa status - exempt application instructions:when applying for the position include with your resume a cover letter explaining:why you are a strong candidate for this positionwhy you are interested in working for rafiki compensation details: 88000-95000 yearly salary

build an american bourbon brand that people genuinely give a sh!t about.this is a hands-on position. you’ll write the plan, then make it happen. new bottle launches. big selling seasons. bar and store displays that earn their space. shooting real ads with real team members on a real lunch break (yes, we did that). and executing ideas that make people say, “wait, a bourbon brand did what now?”you’ll connect the dots across all our partners, while keeping an eye on what actually matters: who knows us, who’s buying us, what they care about, what’s working and what we should do next. you’ll own the budget and the scoreboard too, knowing where to put our money and when it’s time to take a big swing.and you’ll make sure the idea survives all the way to market, from the campaign brief to the sales meeting to the shelf, bar or tailgate where a real bourbon drinker actually sees it. just so you know, we’d much rather debate an idea that makes us uncomfortable than nod politely at a safe one.who you are:you’re a visionary brand builder with a maverick streak. you see where the category is going, where it’s stuck, and where green river has permission to go somewhere else. you have a point of view, you see opportunities other people miss, and you have the ideas and the ability to turn them into work that actually gets into market.you’re equally comfortable with the big idea and the work required to make it real. you can write the brief, build the plan, rally the room, challenge an agency, manage the details and connect creative, social, pr, activation, sales and our partners around a shared ambition.you know when to challenge convention, when to take a calculated risk and when an idea is worth fighting for. you bring people with you, but you don’t need consensus before having a point of view. you’re constantly looking for a better way to work, whether that means ai, new technology or simply refusing to do something the slow way because that’s how it’s always been done.above all, you want ownership. you want the freedom and responsibility to lead green river in disrupting the whiskey space, not just manage the next campaign. if who you are likes who we are, let’s grab a pour and chat. but you must be over 21 to enjoy the pour. (hr made us put this!)   full legal job description including physical requirements available upon request.

metaview is an ai company focused on recruiting. we build ai agents that help world-class companies hire with radically more speed and precision. we automate the toil, and augment the human for companies like brex, affirm, deel, elevenlabs, and airtable.founded by siadhal and shahriar after their experiences scaling uber and palantir, we’ve raised $110m from top-tier investors including google ventures and insight partners.it’s still day 0: now is the time to re-engineer how work gets done with ai at the core, and our toughest challenges still lie ahead. we’re looking for people seeking the hardest, most fulfilling work of their lives.how we workfour principles guide us:velocity. optimize for rate of learning. take action, get feedback, get better. hospitality. sweat the experience. delight customers, candidates and colleagues, even when it’s inconvenient. transparency. public unless private. share context openly within the company so people and agents can take initiative. end-to-end. deliver outcomes, not tasks. step beyond your job description and see the work through. the role:we’re looking for a brand designer to shape how metaview shows up in the world.you’ll work across every expression of our brand, from our website and product launches to campaigns, events, video, and everything in between. you’ll work closely with design, marketing, product, and our founders to turn complex products and ideas into work that feels simple, distinctive, and unmistakably metaview.we care deeply about craft, but also about how we produce it. we’re looking for someone who thinks in systems, gets close to the technology, and builds foundations that help us move faster without lowering the bar.what you'll do:website: maintain and evolve our public site, keeping it sharp, fresh, and differentiated. brand system: evolve metaview’s visual identity and turn it into scalable systems and toolkits across typography, color, illustration, icons, photography, and motion. campaigns & collateral: create standout work across digital, social, print, events, swag, and other brand moments, from concept through production. illustration & graphics: develop distinctive visuals for our website, product experiences, campaigns, and other channels. video: storyboard and direct the visual style of product explainers and brand videos. animation skills are a bonus, not a requirement. presentations: design compelling decks and assets that bring metaview’s story to life. collaboration: partner closely with marketing, product design, video, events, and operations from initial brief through final delivery. what you bring:a strong portfolio showing exceptional brand thinking, visual storytelling, typography, layout, and art direction across digital and physical touchpoints. excellent creative judgment: you can take an ambiguous brief, find the sharpest idea, and turn it into polished, distinctive work. high standards and high velocity: you care deeply about craft, sweat the details, and know when to move quickly. high agency and low ego: you take ownership, work autonomously, collaborate well, and stay hands-on from concept through production. a first-principles mindset and appetite for solving hard creative problems rather than defaulting to what’s been done before. genuine curiosity about ai and excitement to help define the visual language of a company building at the frontier. what we offer:high compensation, through cash and equity. we'll pay for any ai tools & books/resources you need as part of your role. unlimited pto. a ramp card for your wfh setup and the freedom to buy lunch & dinner any time you're in the office. the best co-workers you’ll ever have, in an environment that fosters cohesion, collaboration, and performance. supreme rate-of-learning as we re-orient how the world works with ai.

in 1954, eero saarinen designed a branch office with glass walls, no offices, and a completely open floor plan in columbus, indiana. it was surrounded by trees; the furniture was made by herman miller; the lobby flooring was thick, rustic brick. it was built with transparency and community at its core. since then, a lot of things have happened — saarinen's branch is now a conference center, people increasingly live on the internet, and it's hard to think of a single financial institution that still applies design thinking to their company.mercury is on a mission to defy those expectations. we're a financial technology company that helps startups spend less time banking* and more time building. we believe that the key to our success revolves around thoughtful design — and we hold the craft of that design to an exceptionally high standard. we're looking for a staff brand designer who sets that bar: someone whose eye is so precise, and whose execution is so considered, that the work around them gets better just by virtue of their presence.this is a role for a designer who sweats the details that most people don't notice — the type hierarchy, the negative space, the grid, the crop. someone who has developed a genuine aesthetic philosophy over years of doing hard work at a high level, and who brings that philosophy to everything they touch. you'll own the most technically complex brand design work at mercury, provide craft oversight across the brand studio, and help define what visual excellence looks like as our brand continues to evolve.mercury is a fintech company, not an fdic-insured bank. banking services provided through choice financial group and column n.a., members fdic.in this role, you’ll:set and uphold the craft standard for mercury's brand — across campaigns, web, social, events, and every surface the brand touches.lead the most technically complex and high-visibility brand design projects end-to-end, from brief through delivery.partner with a staff-level brand designer and creative leadership to co-lead the evolution of mercury's creative direction — defining and executing visual standards across typography, imagery, layout, and motion.provide hands-on craft oversight across brand studio output — reviewing work, raising the quality floor, and helping the team make better decisions.commission and art-direct external creatives: photographers, illustrators, and motion designers.develop brand system documentation and decision-making frameworks that help the team move with confidence and consistency.mentor ic3 and ic4 designers through critique, pairing, and direct feedback — elevating their craft through the work, not just in conversation.collaborate with brand strategists, copywriters, pmms, and leadership on how mercury shows up across all channels.shape how brand studio uses ai in its craft. you’ll set the standard for where ai belongs in the creative process, build ai-ready brand guidelines the team can design against, and hold the quality bar as these tools become part of how work gets made.what you’ll bring:a portfolio that is simply excellent — work that demonstrates mastery of typography, layout, color, and composition across a range of brand contexts.a clear and deeply held aesthetic point of view: you can articulate what makes something great and what makes something fall short, and you've built that perspective through years of rigorous practice.fluency in brand systems — you understand how to build for scale and consistency, and you've stewarded a brand through growth or change.7–10+ years of brand design experience, with a background that includes high-craft environments: agency, fashion, elevated consumer, or design-forward tech.experience operating at a staff level: you work autonomously, influence without authority, and make decisions that shape the output of an entire team.proficiency in figma and hands-on experience contributing to or owning a design system.strong verbal and presentation skills — you can communicate the process, intent, and impact of your design decisions with clarity.the judgment to know when to zoom in and when to zoom out, and the discipline to hold both at once.a considered point of view on ai’s place in high-craft design. you’ve used ai tooling in real creative work and can guide a team on where it belongs and how to use it without lowering the bar.curiosity, restraint, and a genuine passion for doing work that's worth doing.mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer. all individuals seeking employment at mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. we are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities or special needs. if you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.total rewardsthe total rewards package at mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options/rsus), and benefits.our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the saas and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. new hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers.our target new hire base salary ranges for this role are the following:us employees in new york city, los angeles, seattle, or the san francisco bay area:$189,400—$236,700 this sector, not settling for doing things as they’ve always been done, but rather looking at how things could be done differently. the agency works on prescription, otc & wellness brands, developing the full range of materials required for communications aimed at healthcare professionals and consumers. the client portfolio spans human and animal health, and a wide range of therapy areas and markets. wherever possible, we bring the most innovative approaches and thinking from the consumer agency to the world of healthcare.the future of healthadvances in technology are driving and changing the way that we all communicate, and whether our target audience is consumers, healthcare professionals or any other stakeholder, integration is now crucial to all marketing communications: at vccp “we believe it only works if it all works”.as part of the vccp partnership, one of the leading consumer agencies, vccp health is perfectly positioned to be leading the way in this new era and transforming healthcare communications.project manager the bigger picturevccp is the global challenger network for challenger brands. with more than 1,500 people across 13 offices in north america, schmidt sciences  is a nonprofit organization founded in 2024 by eric and wendy schmidt that works to accelerate scientific knowledge and breakthroughs with the most promising, advanced tools to support a thriving planet. the organization prioritizes research in areas poised for impact including ai and advanced computing, astrophysics, biosciences, climate, and space—as well as supporting researchers in a variety of disciplines through its science systems program.about the ai & advanced computing center (“ai center”) the ai center at schmidt sciences is a grantmaking and research group that views ai as a transformative force for scientific discovery and societal progress. over the next decade, we aim to support key researchers who are working to make ai systems competent, trustworthy, reliable, and able to effectively partner with human scientists on the next generation of discovery. we will also make selected distinctive investments in beneficial ai areas where philanthropy has a unique advantage. by supporting enabling infrastructure, foundational research and targeted programs in science disciplines, the ai and advanced computing center will create the detail.desc: the foundationwe are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. we believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. we provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. as a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.the teamthe mission of the global policy & advocacy (gpa) division is to understand and shape the public policy debates affecting the foundation's work, build support for its major program and policy objectives, and develop partnerships and alliances that can advance the foundation's objectives nationally and globally. because the foundation's resources alone are not enough to solve the challenges ahead, gpa also supports advocacy efforts to engage diverse collaborators and promote innovative solutions that advance our program goals. we work in close partnership with grantees, our colleagues in the global health, global development, global growth & opportunity, u.s. and gender equality programs and communications to build the environment in which all people have the opportunity to lead healthy and productive lives.requiredglobal program advocacy & communications (gpac) is the foundation’s global capability for issue advocacy and communications. gpac engages where work is cross-market, technically complex, and requires global assets and specialized expertise. working with our program, regional, and country teams, we help mobilize the financing, policy change, and public legitimacy required for impact. gpac’s core functions include: translating program priorities into advocacy strategies and asks: applying deep issue knowledge and policy expertise to translate technical program goals into actionable policy and financing priorities. developing and synthesizing evidence to influence decision-makers: investing in and translating research, data, and technical evidence into investment cases, policy content, and market-ready materials. building and mobilizing advocacy ecosystems: convening and aligning partners, coalitions, and champions to advance policy change, influence agendas, mobilize resources, and strengthen accountability. leading global issue communications: developing evidence-based narratives and communications assets; supporting strategic media engagement and campaigns; and anticipating and managing communications and reputational risks. providing specialized advocacy expertise: offering strategic counsel on complex advocacy challenges to build enabling policy, regulatory, and communications environments. facilitating cross-team collaboration and learning: connecting program, policy, communications, regional, and country teams; sharing intelligence on emerging risks and opportunities; and translating learnings across geographies.gpac partners with foundation colleagues and external stakeholders—including governments, multilateral institutions, civil society, philanthropy, the media, and others—to ensure that global strategies strengthen country-led advocacy and drive measurable progress.your rolethe global health sector is being redefined. development assistance for health has decreased significantly since its peak in 2021, major health multilaterals had difficulty meeting replenishment targets, and bilateral donors are shifting their funding approaches. at the same time, governments in africa and asia are raising domestic health spending and asserting leadership through the lusaka agenda, the accra reset, africa cdc, auda nepad, the african medicines agency, and india’s growing role as a source of vaccines, digital public infrastructure and ai for other countries. ai is moving from pilots into public health systems. the foundation has committed to spend its resources by 2045 to help ensure no mother, child or baby dies of a preventable cause, the next generation grows up in a world without deadly infectious diseases, and hundreds of millions of people break free from poverty.the director, global program advocacy and communications (global pac), health leads the foundation’s global health advocacy through this transition. the director provides strategic leadership for the team that turns the foundation’s health priorities into political will, financing and policy change, and helps build a system of health financing and policy that countries own and that will last beyond any single donor, including the foundation.the director leads global pac health, including the program partner teams aligned to the global health, global development and gender equality divisions, and health communications. the team’s centralized capabilities drive global outcomes and create the narratives, global public goods, evidence, and specialized policy capacity that make market- and country-led advocacy more effective. this includes building investment cases with program and finance and resource mobilization teams, building partner coalitions, crafting issue narratives and spotting risks, and strengthening the policy and regulatory environments needed to advance our health financing and policy goals. the team’s work supports the foundation’s goals and the gpa division priorities that advance them: maternal & child survival, health research and development (r&d), innovation introduction, and health financing.the director works across the foundation with the program strategy teams (psts) and division leadership teams, and across gpa with the market-led teams in europe, middle east and east asia (emeea), north america (nat), africa, india and south/southeast asia, the development policy and finance (dpaf) team, and the philanthropic partnership team (ppt), so that foundation priorities reach decision-makers through strategic, coordinated advocacy. the director leads the team that serves as gpa’s front door to the descriptionamazon’s last-mile delivery network touches millions of customers every day — and with that scale comes real scrutiny. legislation, regulatory shifts, and coordinated advocacy campaigns can delivery operations.as communications manager, last-mile issues and campaigns, you'll own the communications strategy for a portfolio that touches aspects of amazon's last-mile delivery model. managing the reactive moments that come with the portfolio.you're a high-judgment communicator who doesn't flinch when things get complicated. you can hold multiple fast-moving situations at once personalized, tech-enabled education powered by 10,000 faculty and colleagues, covista expands access to healthcare careers and addresses the u.s. healthcare workforce shortage at scale. covista is
