detail.desc: to get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.job categorymarketing & communicationsjob detailsabout salesforcesalesforce is the #1 ai crm, where humans with agents drive customer success together. here, ambition meets action. tech meets trust. and innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. the world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through ai, driving innovation, and keeping salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? you’re in the right place! agentforce is the future of ai, and you are the future of salesforce.the experiencethe global brand & creative (gbc) team within marketing is responsible for our brand and marketing creative. from building brand awareness campaigns to designing experiences like dreamforce, our multi-faceted team does it all. we are a collection of thinkers, makers and doers, whose sole purpose is to bring the brand to life across our incredible portfolio of work.within gbc, the brand insights, strategy & management team is in charge of the brand insights, brand strategy, creative strategy, and brand management that powers the global brand & creative team and salesforce as a whole. we advocate the power of brand across the organization, guide brand marketing activities, and ensure brand excellence.we are looking for a creative strategist who bridges the gap between data-driven market understanding and world-class creative execution. in this role, you will lead the end-to-end creative strategy lifecycle across advertising, sports partnerships, internal campaigns, and events.you will serve as the ultimate connector of dots: identifying what customers and prospects are facing and what they think of us, translating those insights into potent creative strategies that guide our creative teams, and overseeing the validation testing of the resulting creative to ensure it hits the mark. this role will report into the director, creative strategy and work to drive brand awareness and relevance, support wider business objectives, and create strategic alignment across the broader marketing org through influence and relationship-building.what you'll actually be doingown the end-to-end creative lifecycle: manage the continuous loop of generating insights that inform creative strategy, formulating the creative strategy itself, working with creatives to ensure we stay on-brief, and leading the validation testing of the resulting creative.stay on the pulse: spearhead insight and data gathering to understand audience perception and needs. know what the market thinks of us and what audiences need at any given time.differentiate the brand: monitor the competitive landscape to ensure our creative work cuts through the noise, establishing a distinct and powerful brand voice.develop creative strategy: translate data into inspiring, actionable audience insights that inform your creative strategies and briefs across advertising, high-profile sports partnerships, internal employee campaigns, and major events.lead creative testing: guide pre-market and in-market creative testing with our vendors and internal teams to validate concepts, optimize the work, and prove roi.partner across teams: work seamlessly with brand strategy, brand management, and the campaign creative (designers, copywriters, producers) to ensure our high-profile campaigns and marketing activities are strategically sound and creatively compelling.brand advocacy: be a brand advocate within marketing and across salesforce’s global organization.you're our person if...8+ years of experience in creative strategy, brand planning, or creative insights/research roles, with at least 3 years in b2b tech or large-scale global brands.expertise spanning multiple creative disciplines: advertising, sports partnerships, experiential/events, and internal communications.a strong portfolio of creative briefs and strategies that led to measurable business impact and award-winning creative.strong creative instincts rooted in audience understanding and competitive differentiation.excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, capable of influencing creative teams and executive stakeholders. you can “speak creative” and deliver guidance that inspires.strong qualitative and quantitative research skills, with a proven track record of gathering data, uncovering market perceptions, and synthesizing findings into clear strategic narratives.experience designing and leading creative validation and message testing.experience advancing cross-functional initiatives with stakeholders across functions, geographies, and operating units in fast-paced, high-performance environments.ba/bs required; mba a plus.why you are excited about this roleyou always put the customer first.you love living at the intersection of data and creativity, using insights as a springboard for bold ideas.you thrive on variety — from a massive sports partnership campaign one day to an intimate event for c-levels the next.you enjoy the rigor of testing and learning, always seeking to validate and optimize the creative product.you excel at simplifying complexity and providing clear strategic direction.why we are excited about youabove all, you are a sense-maker and a storyteller.you know how to discern between the quality of stories.you have a passion for people and a skill for building relationships with creatives. this role requires a skilled relationship-builder who can create influence across the marketing organization and occasionally with stakeholders outside of marketing to ensure strategic alignment.you are a rare hybrid: deeply analytical but highly creative.you have a keen eye for what makes great creative and the data chops to prove it.you naturally bring out the best in creative teams by providing clear, inspiring, and evidence-backed direction.you are hungry and pro-active; always hunting for the next great unlock.you see brand and creative as a core business driver and can back it up with data.you bring emotional intelligence, balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution, and thrive in ambiguity.you’re an excellent verbal and written communicator; your briefs get to the real heart of it with succinct and powerful words; you never get lost in strategisms or complexity; you can see the center of a concept quickly, clearly, and help others do the same — you make people believe the brand challenge you’re trying to solve.you’re an ai self-starter; experimenting on ways to optimize your own workflows, get to insights faster, and build more expansive and effective processes and ways of working for our team.you can balance big visionary thinking with the simplicity and practicality it takes to ship and ship fast.unleash your potentialwhen you join salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our ai agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. together, we’ll bring the power of agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for ai, and the world.accommodationsif you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this accommodations request form.please note that salesforce uses artificial intelligence (ai) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. please see our candidate privacy statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of ai tools and opt out options.posting statementsalesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. what does that mean exactly? it means that at salesforce, we believe in equality for all. and we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. this policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their salesforce employment journey. it also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at salesforce are fair and based on merit. the same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.in the united states, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. salesforce offers a variety of benefits to help you live well including: time off programs, medical, dental, vision, mental health support, paid parental leave, life and disability insurance, 401(k), and an employee stock purchasing program. more details about company benefits can be found at the following link: https://www.salesforcebenefits.com.at salesforce, we believe in equitable compensation practices that reflect the dynamic nature of labor markets across various regions. the typical base salary range for this position is $143,400 - $216,900 annually. the range represents base salary only, and does not include company bonus, incentive for sales roles, equity or benefits, as applicable.

position summarythe global brand director is a senior global brand and business leader for one of tomy’s major global categories. reporting to the category vice president, this role owns the brand's growth agenda and turns strategy into coordinated action across product, marketing, retail, community, and regions.this role sits at the center of a global ecosystem that may include japan-originated ip, regional teams, commercial partners, licensors, complex launch calendars, and passionate consumer communities. the director must connect those groups around a clear direction while staying close to the realities of the product, consumer, customer, and market.the director is the senior integrator for the portfolio, aligning brand strategy, product roadmap, commercial priorities, creative direction, community strategy, and regional execution. they partner closely with category leadership, japan, commercial, npd & innovation, consumer insights, finance, operations, legal, and marketing shared services.success requires both strategic altitude and hands-on ownership. this leader frames the choices that matter, stays close to the work, acts with urgency, and brings the humility to learn from others.key responsibilities1. global brand strategy & architecturedefine the assigned brand's purpose, positioning, target consumer, value proposition, architecture, growth ambition, and role in the category portfolio - and ensure that direction is visible across product, content, community, retail, and communications.build annual and multi-year brand plans grounded in consumer, shopper, community, category, cultural, competitive, ip, and performance insight.stay close to consumers, communities, retail, culture, and regional teams. turn those signals into sharper brand, product, and commercial choices.set global brand guardrails, claims, tone, visual and content principles, product hierarchy, and channel roles; make clear what must remain consistent globally and where markets have room to adapt.2. portfolio, innovation & lifecycle roadmapown the brand / product roadmap, innovation briefs, renovation priorities, line extensions, seasonal opportunities, and lifecycle recommendations, connecting consumer needs and play behavior to product opportunity.build deep product fluency. partner with npd, insights, product integrity, ip / japan, manufacturing pmo, and supply chain on value, feasibility, timing, cost, and compliance. challenge assumptions when the consumer or business case demands it.provide pricing architecture, assortment, hero-product, exclusivity, and launch-priority inputs in partnership with category leadership, regional commercial teams, and brand finance.recommend where to invest, accelerate, optimize, rationalize, or discontinue - balancing growth, margin, brand equity, consumer value, and long-term franchise health.3. launch, campaign & content directiontranslate strategy into inspiring launch briefs, campaign objectives, target-consumer direction, key messages, content requirements, asset plans, and global toolkits that teams can actually use.lead marketing services and agency partners with clear briefs and decisive feedback; raise the creative bar and ensure work is strategically right, culturally relevant, complete, reusable, and region-ready.connect product, packaging, ip / licensor needs, content, fandom, community, partnerships, retail activation, and launch calendars into one coherent consumer experience.use post-launch learning, retailer feedback, and consumer and community response to improve quickly. build repeat engagement, advocacy, and long-term fandom - not just one-time launch awareness.4. regional & commercial enablementpartner with regional heads of marketing to co-create local plans, cultural and language adaptation, trade / shopper activation, and market calendars while protecting a clear global strategic center.equip sales and regional teams with strong category and brand stories, launch priorities, customer materials, product narratives, and channel guidance that build retailer confidence and unlock growth.clarify global guardrails: what should remain consistent, where local adaptation adds value, and where teams need tighter alignment.actively seek regional, customer, and market feedback, close the loop, and use it to improve global strategy, product, content, and activation rather than treating localization as a one-way handoff.5. brand economics & performance managementpartner with brand finance on the brand p&l, pricing, margin, royalty, promotion, marketing investment, innovation economics, and the choices required to improve profitable growth.create a focused view of performance across consumer, community, commercial, financial, digital, retail, and launch indicators. make the implications clear.diagnose root causes behind performance gaps, separate signal from noise, and recommend focused corrective action with urgency and discipline.balance brand equity, consumer value, sales, margin, inventory, and long-term franchise health. know when to protect the brand, push for growth, or invest for disproportionate return.6. cross-functional leadership & brand stewardshipserve as the primary global point of accountability for the assigned brand across category leadership, japan / ip, regions, commercial, operations, growth ventures, finance, legal, and marketing shared services.lead through influence, preparation, and trust. challenge respectfully, resolve unclear handoffs, make recommendations with conviction, and escalate material decisions at the right time.create simple operating rhythms that keep decisions, actions, assets, and learning visible across functions, regions, and time zones.coach and develop talent while modeling curiosity, humility, accountability, collaboration, consumer passion, and a bias for action.qualificationsexperience8-10+ years of progressive brand, marketing, or consumer-business leadership experience at a scope appropriate to a global director role.proven success building and growing consumer brands or franchises across product, marketing, retail, content, community, and multiple markets.significant experience in toys or a closely adjacent fandom-driven category is required. relevant adjacencies include gaming, collectibles, entertainment, sports, licensed consumer products, and youth culture.strong cross-cultural leadership. experience with japanese headquarters, japanese partners, or japan-originated ip is highly valued.low-ego people leadership with strong creative, commercial, and analytical judgment. able to coach talent, influence senior leaders, and operate effectively in ambiguity.education & credentialsbachelor's degree or equivalent experience. advanced credentials are welcome; demonstrated judgment, learning agility, and results matter more.skills & capabilitiesbrand strategy, positioning, architecture, franchise storytelling, portfolio roadmaps, and lifecycle management.deep consumer, shopper, community, and cultural insight - including the ability to build fandom, deepen engagement, drive repeat participation, and turn consumers into advocates.product curiosity and innovation judgment, from strong briefs and product evaluation through launch planning and consumer experience.commercial and financial acumen across pricing, margin, assortment, retail dynamics, marketing investment, inventory, and channel roles.cross-cultural matrix leadership: build trust, adapt communication style, create clarity across working norms, and influence across japan, regions, and functions without creating bureaucracy.a proactive, hands-on builder mindset with compelling storytelling, agency leadership, learning agility, resourcefulness, and notably low ego.success measuresnet sales, gross margin, market share, brand health, and long-term franchise relevance.innovation and launch success, time-to-market, lifecycle productivity, and quality of the consumer experience.consumer and community growth, repeat engagement, advocacy, cultural relevance, and retailer / regional confidence in the brand.effective pricing, assortment, inventory, and marketing investment - plus strong trust and execution across japan, regions, commercial, and cross-functional partners.

job summaryinsulet is on a mission to simplify life for people living with diabetes! we are looking for a senior ux content strategist to join our growing user experience (ux) team and help accomplish this mission. apply your strategic, organizational, and creative skills to provide engaging, informative content that is vital to our products and customer experience. a strong background in content strategy or content production is required.the senior ux content strategist is a highly collaborative role in which you'll partner with multiple cross-functional teams distributed around the globe. the senior content strategist, instructional design, is responsible for creating both long- and short-form instructional content for user guides and in-app help. you'll also use your editorial expertise to ensure all user guide content remains on brand, adheres to our voice and tone guidelines, and meets literacy-level requirements.you will work closely with instructional design and ux leadership to coordinate content strategy and production. the ideal candidate is a strategic thinker with significant experience driving innovation by connecting the dots, building processes, and adapting to changing priorities. they should be able to balance independent judgment with cross-functional collaboration while developing effective methods and processes to achieve results.responsibilitiescontent development and maintenance: ensure all content is consistent in terms of brand, style, voice and tone, quality, and literacy/grade levels across all products/platforms. collaborate frequently with cross-functional stakeholders on software and hardware releases, new features, new products, regulatory submissions, and commercial launches. this includes collaborating with: cross-functional product teams to assess the impact of their features and requirements on existing user guide and in-app help content and develop new user guides or sets of in-app help to support new products. regulatory and medical affairs to incorporate regulatory requirements and medical guidance as needed. systems engineering and compliance to ensure all product requirements are met in the instructions for use (ifus). explain concepts and features in simple, layperson language (8th grade level or below), tailoring your writing style to various age groups and audiences to maximize content retention. organize and drive timely reviews and iterations with all subject matter experts and stakeholders (both internal and external) of all instructional documents being developed, particularly with ux, medical, and human factors. facilitate user guide drafts for human factors testing to demonstrate that instructional material is easy to understand, learning objectives are achieved, and use error risks are reduced. strategystrategize and define logic for help content across various projects. lead, execute, and advise on ux content strategy. adhere to existing processes, while evangelizing content best practices and processes across cross-functional groups. propose process and tool improvements and support evaluating future tools. quality processesmaintain, in a detailed and organized manner, the electronic libraries of all materials used in the development of instructional materials from development phases through release to production. ensure efficient release and quality hand-off of outputs to labeling and doc control teams for timely review, approval, and sustained design control and production. responsible for content submissions into product lifecyle management (plm) systems and reviewing the work of others. actively participate on improvements to sops and on general advancements of processes for operational efficiency and effectiveness. ensure design, review, production, and maintenance methods and processes are consistent and follow/support the quality policy, as well as all iso quality system procedures and guidelines. conduct design reviews and participate in pi planning and engineering design review meetings as required. report on all tasks and progress on execution following organizational practices and standards established by program management and project leadership. support and maintain documentation links between insulet and all external partners. required qualificationsbachelor’s degree or equivalent industry experience. 5+ years of experience in ux content strategy, technical writing, ux writing, or content design. exceptional writing and editing capabilities. effective project management and multitasking skills. experience managing multiple stakeholders and multiple projects though different stages of content production or strategy. familiarity with common authoring tools, design tools, language, and processes. experience working in single-sourcing strategies. preferred qualificationsbachelor’s degree in communications, writing, english, health or a similar field, from an accredited four-year university, or equivalent experience. extensive experience in content management solutions in a technical context (e.g. web and mobile apps). experience working with structured content, dita xml, or a component content management system. experience developing and defining content strategy, including content management and operations solutions and processes, especially experience administering an authoring tool or cms. experience in healthcare, pharmaceutical, medical device industries or another highly regulated industry. experience working in jira, confluence, figma, adobe creative cloud or similar tools. understanding of agile/safe planning processes (certification optional). passion for making a positive impact in people’s lives. empathy for the audiences we serve. physical requirementsoccasional us travel, as needed (semi-annually)this position is eligible for hybrid working arrangements and requires on-site work from an insulet office. additional informationcompensation & benefits: for u.s.-based positions only, the annual base salary range for this role is $118,900.00 - $178,300.00 this position may also be eligible for incentive compensation. we offer a comprehensive benefits package, including: medical, dental, and vision insurance 401(k) with company match paid time off (pto) and additional employee wellness programs application details: this job posting will remain open until the position is filled. to apply, please visit the insulet careers site and submit your application online. actual pay depends on skills, experience, and education.insulet corporation (nasdaq: podd), headquartered in massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its omnipod product platform. the omnipod insulin management system provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. with its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. insulet’s flagship innovation, the omnipod 5 automated insulin delivery system, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the u.s. or by the omnipod 5 controller. insulet also leverages the unique design of its pod by tailoring its omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. for more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.we are looking for highly motivated, performance-driven individuals to be a part of our expanding team. we do this by hiring amazing people guided by shared values who exceed customer expectations. our continued success depends on it!at insulet corporation all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.(know your rights)

detail.desc: position summarysdsu is seeking a college of engineering media relations officer with experience in media relations and journalistic science writing — identifying newsworthy research and translating complex findings into clear, accurate, and engaging stories for general audiences. to help tell the stories emerging from the university’s research enterprise, with a particular focus on the college of engineering, the media relations officer will help tell the stories emerging from the university’s research enterprise. under the direction of the senior director of media relations and deputy chief communications officer, work directly with researchers, faculty, university leaders, reporters, and fellow communicators to translate complex ideas into compelling stories and help those stories reach audiences locally, nationally, and internationally.this is a hands-on communications role with plenty of variety. one day, you may be interviewing a researcher, writing about a new discovery and pitching the story to national media; another, you may be developing a communications plan as part of a college-wide initiative, preparing a faculty member for an interview, responding to a media inquiry, or creating multimedia and social media content. you will also monitor news and online conversations, assess emerging issues and reputational risks, and recommend messaging and communications strategies.what you’ll doresearch storytelling & contentfind compelling stories across sdsu’s research enterprise, particularly in engineering, science, and technology. translate complex research into clear, engaging stories for sdsu newscenter, sdsu magazine, websites, social media, external media pitching, and other channels. develop multimedia and short-form content that expands the reach of research stories. media relationsdevelop targeted pitches, news releases, media advisories, and communications plans. build relationships with regional, national, and international reporters and identify opportunities to connect sdsu experts with the news. coordinate interviews and prepare faculty and staff for media engagement. respond to media inquiries and develop recommended messaging and statements. college of engineering communicationsserve as a key communications partner to college of engineering faculty and leadership. identify stories, develop communications strategies, and coordinate media relations, editorial, and social media efforts. develop the college of engineering newsletter collaborate across stratcomm and with campus communications partners to keep messaging aligned. issues & emerging communicationsmonitor news and social media for emerging issues, misinformation, and reputational concerns. draft holding statements, faqs, reactive messaging, and communications recommendations. balance proactive storytelling with the real-time communications needs of a large public research university. what we’re looking forwe’re looking for an experienced communicator who can move comfortably between journalistic science writing, media relations and strategic communications. you should be able to interview researchers and translate complex scientific and technical information into clear, accurate and compelling stories for general audiences. this is not a grant writing or technical writing role. you should be able to make complicated subjects accessible, recognize a strong story, build relationships with reporters, manage competing priorities, and exercise good judgment when issues move quickly.above all, this role is for someone who is curious enough to dig into a complicated subject, confident enough to ask the follow-up question, and adaptable enough to switch gears when the story changes.as part of the california state university (csu) system, san diego state university helps power one of the largest and most impactful public university systems in the nation. see what it’s like to work at the csu—watch our video and imagine your future here: working at the csu .position informationthis is a full-time (1.0 time-base), benefits eligible, permanent/probationary position. this position is designated as exempt under flsa and is not eligible for overtime compensation. standard sdsu work hours are monday – friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but may vary based on operational needs. the position is approved for partial telecommuting with onsite work at the san diego campus on monday and wednesday. please note that the incumbent will be called to campus on telecommuting days to support campus activities as needed. department summarysan diego state university (sdsu) is a leading public research university within the california state university system, serving more than 46,000 students. sdsu is recognized for its academic excellence, research, innovation, global engagement, and commitment to student success.the president serves as the university’s chief executive officer, providing leadership for sdsu’s academic mission, operations, and strategic priorities. the office of the president supports the president in carrying out these executive responsibilities and advancing the university’s goals.strategic communications and public affairs (stratcomm) serves as the official voice of sdsu, sharing the president’s vision, values, and priorities and telling the university’s story to campus and external audiences. stratcomm leads communications across marketing, media relations, social media, web and digital communications, executive and internal communications, crisis and issues management, visual communications, and government and community relations. the department also manages and protects the sdsu brand and works with partners across the university to highlight sdsu’s programs, achievements, and impact.for more information regarding the strategic communications and public affairs (stratcomm) department, click here .education and experienceequivalent to a bachelor’s degree in a related field and four years of relevant experience. additional experience which demonstrates acquired and successfully applied knowledge and abilities shown above may be substituted for the required education on a year-for-year basis. an advanced degree in a related field may be substituted for the required experience on a year-for-year basis.key qualificationsdemonstrated experience in strategic communications, media relations, and science or research communications, preferably within a large organization. exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex scientific, engineering, and technical information into clear, compelling content for broad audiences. proven success developing media strategies, building relationships with reporters, and securing earned media coverage at the regional, national, or international level. experience advising executives, faculty, researchers, or subject-matter experts on media engagement, strategic messaging, issues management, and reputational considerations. ability to develop and execute integrated communications across earned media, digital, social, editorial, and multimedia channels. demonstrated ability to independently manage complex, cross-functional communications projects, balance competing priorities, and collaborate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders. experience using media analytics, audience insights, and performance data to evaluate communications efforts and inform strategy. strong knowledge of communications and editorial best practices, including ap style. preferred qualifications: experience supporting science, research, engineering, or technology communications within higher education, a research institution, public agency, or similarly complex organization. knowledge of higher education communications and the research environment, particularly within a public research university. professional proficiency in spanish is desirable. licenses/certifications requiredvalid california driver’s license or the ability to obtain one within 30 days of hire.compensation and benefitssan diego state university offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and professional growth.compensationstep placement will be determined based on relevant qualifications and professional experience, in alignment with the department’s budget and equity guidelines.initial step placement is not expected to exceed step 1 ($5,877/month). salary step placement for internal applicants will follow the csueu collective bargaining agreement. csu classification salary range: $5,877-$8,561 per month (step 1-step 20). future increases, including step advancements, are subject to contract negotiations. full benefits package includesgenerous time off: 15 paid holidays, vacation, and sick leave. retirement: calpers pension plan with retiree healthcare, and reciprocal agreements with other california public retirement systems, including the uc. health coverage: medical, dental, and vision options at low or no cost. education support: csu tuition fee waiver for employees and eligible dependents. optional offerings: flexcash, life and disability insurance, legal and pet plans. campus & community: access to the library, campus events, employee groups, and volunteer and social activities. our benefits are a significant part of total compensation. learn more at the sdsu benefits overview .sdsu valuesat sdsu, detail.desc: director, communicationsfull-time fas staffwashington, dcwhy fas?  does fas sound like an organization that you would be energized to join?  is it aligned to your values?the federation of american scientists (fas) takes quite seriously our role as a beacon and voice for the science community.  fas has a rich history: after the devastating bombings of hiroshima and nagasaki in 1945, a group of atomic researchers – deeply concerned about the use of science for malice – created an organization committed to using science and technology to benefit humanity.  the group they created – the federation of atomic scientists – soon became the federation of american scientists in recognition of the hundreds of scientists across diverse disciplines who joined together to speak with one voice for the betterment of the world.  today, we are a group of entrepreneurial, intrepid changemakers, forging a better future for all through the nexus of science, technology and talent. we value equity, inclusion, and transparency.  as a collective, we are building an organization focused on being impact-driven, customer-focused, and growth-oriented as a force for good in the world.skills and expertise: must haveswhat skills do you need to show proficiency (or higher) in order to be a strong candidate?skillswhat skills do you need to possess to be a strong candidate?experience building and managing relationships with national press, with a track record of securing earned media coverage in top-tier outlets.ability to manage and hone a public brand, including digital assets.experience building and managing working relationships with policy leads, technical experts, and executive leadership, including aligning their priorities with institutional communications goals and giving candid, constructive feedback.a demonstrated commitment to sound leadership: experience coaching and developing a team and directing a network of outside consultants and vendors. a proven track record developing and executing strategic communications plans, ideally in a policy, nonprofit, think tank, or advocacy environment.sharp editorial judgment with the ability to translate complex technical and scientific research into clear, compelling narratives for media, policymakers, and the public.strong strategic prioritization skills and connecting individual campaigns into a single institutional narrative.comfort working within an existing editorial and campaign process rather than building one from scratch and the judgment to know what to add versus what to leave alone.excellent written and verbal communication skills, with high attention to detail.expertisewhat skills do you need to show proficiency (or higher) in order to be a strong candidate?13+ years of communications experience, including at least 3 years in a senior or leadership capacity.demonstrated expertise in policy communications, media relations, or public affairs, ideally in a washington, dc context.a track record of measurable impact: audience growth, message pickup and earned media, or campaign results tied to organizational goals.familiarity with the science and technology policy landscape and policy entrepreneurship is a strong plus.experience operating at the strategic layer above day-to-day content production by setting priorities across a portfolio of projects.supporting and growing communications campaigns from idea to execution.to sum it up…what’s the “elevator pitch” for the role?fas is looking for a strategic communications leader, someone who can turn cutting-edge science and technology research into a national narrative that moves policymakers, press, and the public. fas's communications team already runs a strong project-level operation and includes an editorial calendar, a structured launch process, and campaign execution. what we are looking for is the layer above it: someone to prioritize across projects, set organizational messaging priorities and the institutional narrative, build relationships with top-tier national outlets, and unify individual campaigns into one fas narrative. if you want to elevate an already strong communications operation into a national brand, inside an organization with an 80-year history of scientific credibility and real policy influence in washington, this is a rare opportunity to shape the story at the highest level.work environment this position will be a hybrid role, meaning that both remote and in-person work can be accommodated, generally two to three days per week on-site and two to three days per week remote. for this role, much of the work will be relationship building and meeting with national press, policymakers, and partner organizations within washington, dc.this position manages some employees in a union-represented collective bargaining unit, and specific terms and conditions of employment are subject to collective bargaining.salary range$180,000 - 200,000benefitsfas offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package that supports employees’ health, financial security, and overall well-being. benefits include a competitive 403(b) retirement plan, medical, dental, and vision coverage, short-term and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, employee assistance support, pre-tax benefits such as healthcare and dependent care fsas, and commuter benefits.hiring statementdon’t check off every box? apply anyway! studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every listed qualification. at fas we are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, and developing new voices. if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly, we encourage you to apply anyway – you might just be the right candidate.the federation of american scientists is an equal opportunity employer. all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, amnesty, or status as a covered veteran in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws. the federation of american scientists prohibits discriminating against employees and job applicants who inquire about, discuss, or disclose the compensation of the employee or applicant or another employee or applicant. employment is contingent on successful verification of eligibility to work in the united states.

unchained at last, the survivor-led nonprofit at the helm of the national movement to end forced and child marriage in the united states, has grown to the point that it now seeks a communications director to be the architect of unchained's public voice — building the organization's narrative strategy, managing media relationships and ensuring that survivor stories are told with power, accuracy and care. warning: apply for this position only if you want a deeply meaningful, adventure-filled job that makes all your friends jealous.job descriptionthe communications director will ensure that unchained’s messaging reaches its intended audiences and produces its intended effect. reporting to the executive director, the communications director will get the opportunity to:develop robust, creative communications strategies;manage unchained’s communications staff and contractors as they implement the strategies;oversee and create content for:unchained’s website, eblasts and social media channelspress releasesgrant proposals, fundraising appeals and annual reportspolicy memosdraft compelling messaging for various audiences and platforms;build relationships with news media and track media coverage;prepare the executive director and survivor allies for interviews and legislative testimony; andmonitor analytics across unchained’s various platforms and adjust accordingly.qualificationsyou might be a good fit for this position if you:have at least seven years of relevant professional experience in communications, public relations, development or a related field, in the nonprofit sector;have successfully placed stories in major media outlets;write exceptionally well; andfeel passionately about unchained’s mission.bonus qualificationsmake sure to note in your application if you:have experience writing policy memos. unchained encourages survivors of forced marriage to apply.note: an internal study at hp found women applied for a promotion only if they met 100 percent of the qualifications, while men applied if they met 60 percent. regardless of your gender, if you are excited about this job, go for it — even if you do not meet 100 percent of the qualifications.salary/benefitsthe compensation package for this position includes:salary of $140,000;401(k) retirement plan with employer match;high-quality health insurance;dental insurance;vision insurance;life insurance;long-term disability insurance;flexible spending account so you can pay certain health and commuter costs pre-tax;mostly remote work;generous paid time off, including parental leave;solid work-life balance (the workday ends at 5:00 p.m. — and earlier on fridays — except in emergencies);monthly art therapy sessions with the unchained team; andunited nations grounds pass.locationremote (eastern time). about unchaineda lifetime of rape, forced parenthood, financial dependence and domestic servitude. this is the reality for individuals in the united states whose lives are ripped apart by forced marriage.unchained is the only organization dedicated to providing comprehensive, often life-saving legal and social services and emotional support — always for free — to individuals in the u.s. who are resisting or escaping forced marriage. unchained also is the only organization dedicated to promoting social, policy and legal change to end forced and child marriage in the u.s. the organization started and now leads a growing national movement to end child marriage in every u.s. state and at the federal level.a day at unchained is rarely dull. members of the small but feisty unchained team travel all across the u.s. to testify at legislative hearings and to chain-in, in bridal gowns and chains, to protest forced and child marriage. in just the last few years, team members ate dinner with chelsea clinton, watched multiple broadway shows and appeared on apple tv’s gutsy series.unchained prioritizes self-care and team building. the virtual office closes early every friday and every day during the last week of the year and closes for all federal holidays and for a week every summer – in addition to a generous paid-time-off package. the unchained team holds monthly art therapy sessions and semi-annual staff retreats that sometimes involve wearing pajamas to the office and always involve eating too much guacamole.how to applyto be considered for this position, submit your application and resume at https://unchainedatlast.org/application-for-employment. you will receive a confirmation email letting you know your application was received.an unchained team member will reach out if you seem to be a good fit for the open position. you will then have the chance to advance through unchained's multi-step interview process, which typically takes a couple of weeks.tips for a successful applicationif you really want this position, these tips might help:how are you perfect for this role? make that clear in your application, rather than assuming it is obvious from your resume.does your resume have gaps or anything that might cause confusion? best to explain those in your application.have you reviewed the unchained website? you will deeply impress your interviewers if you are deeply familiar with the organization.not sure whether to send a "thank you" after an interview? the answer is always yes. the unchained team appreciates appreciation.

detail.desc: at ey, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.we’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. join ey and help to build a better working world.the brand, marketing and communications (bmc) function plays a critical role in achieving ey’s ambition to create long-term value as the world’s most trusted, distinctive professional services organization.through the collective power of bmc – which includes responsibility for content development, editorial and syndication through paid, owned, and earned media; webcast and live event staging; and campaign strategy, planning, and operations – we work hand in hand with ey teams to take solutions and services to market, bring our purpose of building a better working world to life, engage our people, and build the commercial value and emotional resonance of the ey brand.the opportunity client technology (ct) is at the heart of ey’s growth ambition, responsible for working with ey businesses and alliance partners to develop the global products, platforms and standards that help elevate the ey service offering, win in the market and deliver confidence to clients. as technology becomes an increasingly important driver of business transformation, enterprise resilience and client confidence, effective communication and engagement are critical to realizing the value that ct delivers.as a communications and engagement lead within the ct bmc team, you will lead the global communications, engagement and adoption strategy to shape how technologists in ey understand, trust and adopt the platforms, standards and capabilities that ct provides. you will be responsible for translating complex technology and transformation priorities into clear, compelling narratives that inspire action, drive behavior change and strengthen confidence in ct across the organization.this is a senior, high-impact role at the heart of ey's ai-first transformation. acting as a trusted advisor to ct leadership, including the ct operating committee and the global vice chair – client technology, you will shape executive communications, influence strategic decisions, and help ensure ct communicates with clarity, consistency and confidence at the moments that matter most.you will also play a critical role in strengthening ct's position as one of ey's most compelling client zero stories, helping technologists and client-serving teams understand how ey applies its own technology capabilities to create business value and build confidence with clients.this role requires a strategic communications leader who thrives in a fast-paced, complex, global environment and can influence senior stakeholders, navigate ambiguity, and drive measurable business outcomes through communications, engagement and adoption strategies.your key responsibilities strategic communications and engagement leadership: own and evolve the global communications, engagement and adoption strategy for ey global standards, our ey fabric technology platform and operations and support capabilities, to strengthen the security and scalability of ey technology and deliver confidence to help ey client servers win in the market.executive advisory and leadership communications: act as a trusted communications advisor to ct senior leadership, including members of the ct operating committee and the global vice chair – client technology. provide strategic counsel on executive positioning, organizational change, transformation initiatives, leadership engagement and complex communications challenges. serve as deputy to the ct bmc leader on communications and engagement activities.global narrative, positioning and message architecture: lead the development of global positioning, messaging and narrative frameworks for ct's capabilities, standards, platforms and strategic initiatives, working with g&i bmc leads, including the tech marketing lead and platform marketing lead, to ensure alignment with broader technology messaging. partner closely with global, region and service line bmc teams and stakeholders to ensure consistent, audience-centric communications and alignment across ey.adoption and change communications: design and execute engagement strategies that accelerate adoption of ct standards, platforms and strategic capabilities. apply change management and behavior change principles to help drive secure, scalable and consistent technology development practices across the global ey technologist community.transformation campaign leadership: lead integrated communications for ct's most significant transformation priorities and emerging technology capabilities. set strategic direction for complex global campaigns, balancing long-term engagement objectives with rapid-response support for high-visibility business, technology and leadership moments.knowledge sharing: facilitate knowledge sharing across the ey technologist community that promote the skillsets, mindsets and toolsets required to be a technologist of the future. propose original channels and communications that resonate with target audiences, and reflect ct’s position as ai-first technology experts within ey.insight, measurement and performance optimization: conduct adoption analysis and audience segmentation to identify gaps and inform internal marketing strategies and campaigns. establish and lead the ct bmc measurement framework, defining success metrics that demonstrate business impact and communication effectiveness. leverage audience insights, adoption analytics and performance data to optimize strategy, improve engagement and guide investment decisions.operating model and team leadership: lead and develop the ct content delivery team, building a high-performing communications capability that supports ct's global objectives. define and continuously improve communication processes, governance, templates, channels and measurement practices, embedding a scalable and data-driven approach across ct bmc.skills and attributes for successexecutive presence and strategic influence: demonstrated experience advising and influencing senior leaders within large, highly matrixed global organizations. ability to build credibility quickly, challenge constructively and operate as a trusted advisor at executive level.strategic communications leadership: extensive experience developing enterprise-wide communications strategies that support transformation, adoption and business change. proven ability to align communication activity to measurable organizational outcomes.global stakeholder management: exceptional ability to build relationships, navigate complexity and influence diverse stakeholder groups across functions, geographies and leadership levels.storytelling and communication excellence: outstanding storytelling, editorial and executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technology and transformation concepts into compelling narratives tailored to diverse audiences. exceptional attentional to detail.change and adoption expertise: strong understanding of change communications, engagement strategies and behavior change principles, with experience driving adoption and engagement at scale.data-driven decision making: strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities, with the ability to derive actionable insights from audience, engagement and adoption data and translate them into communications strategies that deliver measurable impact.digital and ai fluency: strong understanding of emerging technologies, digital channels, ai enabled communications and innovative engagement approaches. demonstrated ability to leverage technology to improve reach, relevance, efficiency and impact.leadership and team development: experience leading high-performing teams, setting strategic direction, building capability and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and collaboration.global experience: extensive experience leading and working with global, cross-border communications initiatives, successfully managing multiple complex programmes and stakeholders across geographies, leveraging a strong network.what we look forwe’re looking for a senior communications professional who embraces technology, brings curiosity and energy, and works collaboratively with leaders and teams to deliver meaningful engagement.what we offer youthe compensation ranges below are provided in order to comply with united states pay transparency laws. other geographies will follow their local salary guidelines, which may not be a direct conversion of published us salary ranges. at ey, we harness our collective strength to empower you to shape your future with confidence through professional growth, personal fulfillment and an inclusive culture. learn more at ey.com/us/careers.we offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to the business. the base salary range for this job is:new york city, boston, and washington dc metro areas, washington state, and southern california offices – $154,300 to $277,700bay area california offices – $160,700 to $289,300all other offices locations in the us, including sacramento – $128,600 to $254,600individual salaries within these ranges are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge, skills and geography. in addition, our total rewards package includes medical and dental coverage, pension and 401(k) plans, and a wide range of paid time off options.under our flexible vacation policy, you’ll decide how much vacation time you need based on your own personal circumstances. you’ll also be granted time off for designated ey paid holidays, winter/summer breaks, personal/family care, and other leaves of absence when needed to support your physical, financial, and emotional well-being.are you ready to shape your future with confidence? apply today. to make the most of your application experience, please limit yourself to two applications within a six-month period.ey accepts applications for this position on an on-going basis.for those living in california, please click here for additional information.at ey, our values set the foundation for how we work and the behaviors we expect of our people. any misrepresentation or falsification of information or lack of integrity at any point in the recruiting process may result in withdrawal of your candidacy, revocation of an offer or immediate termination of employment.ey | building a better working worldey is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.enabled by data, ai and advanced technology, ey teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.ey teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, ey teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.all in to shape the future with confidence.ey national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected basis, including arrest and conviction records, in accordance with applicable law. ey is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities including veterans with disabilities. if you have a disability and either need assistance applying online or need to request an accommodation during any part of the application process, please call 1-800-ey-help3, select option 2 for candidate related inquiries, then select option 1 for candidate queries and finally select option 2 for candidates with an inquiry which will route you to ey’s talent shared services team (tss) or email the tss at ssc.customersupport@ey.com.

grow community transit’s employer program as a marketing program strategist!partner with employers to create greener, easier, and more sustainable commutes.do you care about reducing pollution and road congestion in your community? at community transit, we're looking for a marketing program strategist to help grow our employer-focused programs. in this role, you'll join our marketing programs team and partner with businesses to reduce the drive-alone rate of their employees.what's the role?as a marketing program strategist, you'll partner with major employers to encourage and incentivize workers to use transit for commuting to work and other everyday travel. programs include commute trip reduction (ctr), orca for business, and local incentive programs to engage a diverse range of employers and workers throughout our community.some projects we’re planning…the successful candidate will be responsible for managing our portfolio of major employers, helping them establish worksite programs that achieve commute trip reduction goals and engage employees with sustainable travel options.review public records and develop other sources to identify major employers affected by washington’s commute trip reduction program and help bring them into compliance with state and local requirements.convene and facilitate a countywide ctr planning process that supports snohomish county jurisdictions in developing aligned and mutually reinforcing four‑year ctr plans.help design and pilot a new recognition program to evaluate and celebrate employers who implement effective commute trip reduction strategies at their worksites.who are we looking for?we need someone who will:be driven to make a difference in our community with tenacity and grit. find opportunities for improvement and take initiative to meet goals and grow programs. take ownership of programs and continuously improve them over time. work independently while maintaining a strong and consistent presence within an inclusive, collaborative, and dynamic team of program owners. build and maintain strong relationships through regular in-person engagement with employers, workers, the public, stakeholders, and colleagues. design and implement strategies to continuously engage businesses and workers. use transportation demand management (tdm) strategies to educate people and inspire behavior change. understand and promote sustainable transportation modes that are complementary to transit. encourage and inspire people to use transit for work commutes and everyday travel. why join community transit?at community transit, we help people get from where they are to where they want to be. we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diversity and individual differences are valued and leveraged. we offer generous compensation and benefits, opportunities for professional growth, and a flexible hybrid work environment that balances remote work with meaningful in-person teamwork and community engagement.ready to apply?if you're excited about this opportunity and ready to contribute to our mission, we want to hear from you! join us at community transit and help shape the future of transportation in our community.essential dutieskey responsibilities:create informative, inclusive, and engaging program content and strategies. ensure program activities are in alignment with community transit’s goals and values. create project management plans, timelines, task lists, budgets, and other documentation to ensure projects are tracked and delivered successfully. create marketing event and campaign proposals and plans, briefs, budgets, presentations, project calendars, and post-campaign evaluations. set, track, and report on the program’s key performance indicators (kpis) and identify areas for improvement. integrate industry best practices and your creative innovations. build and maintain relationships internally, across community transit departments, and externally with residents, schools, businesses, community organizations, event venues, state agencies, etc. act as a subject matter expert on program marketing and ridership. offer insight to stakeholders, as requested. lead and contribute to cross-functional project teams. assist the broader marketing team with projects and events, as needed. perform other duties of a similar nature or level. requirementsminimum qualifications5 years of experience working in or related to one of the following areas:events management, strategy, or planning commute trip reduction (ctr)transportation demand management (tdm)communications, marketing, or sales (b2b, b2b2c)3 years of experience planning and executing medium-scale events (51-100 attendees). 1 year of experience using client relationship management (crm) systems such as salesforce. proficiency with microsoft office tools. ability to work weekends, holidays, and extended hours, as needed. an equivalent combination of education and experience to successfully perform the job duties is also accepted.knowledge requirementsinclusive marketing practices and techniques. promotional strategies. leveraging various communication channels to engage with the public. grammar rules. problem assessment and process improvement methods. budget management. vendor management. insurance, legal, health, and safety regulations and standards for events. skill requirementsfostering an inclusive workplace by upholding community transit’s core values in support of theorganization’s vision and mission. inspiring team commitment, pride, and trust while promotingcooperation and motivating members to achieve shared goals. demonstrating courtesy, sensitivity,and respect in all interactions. excellent writing and editing ability. collaborating cross-functionally with strong interpersonal communication. public speaking and presenting. effectively managing time and project schedules, including coordinating meetings, assigned actions,and due dates. ability to negotiate and influence others to achieve business goals and core values. project management. maintaining objectivity and using data to inform collaborative decision making. compiling, analyzing, and preparing spreadsheets and reports. professional experience with pc-based software such as ms office, email, and scheduling applications. preferred knowledge and skillsbachelor's degree in marketing, communications, business administration, public administration, urban planning, or a related field. proficiency in smartsheet or similar cloud-based project management and collaboration tools. experience applying transportation demand management (tdm) strategies. familiarity with community transit and transit industry products, services, networks, agencies, and issues. fluency in another language in addition to english. working conditionshybrid telework may be available. availability is at management discretion and may not be available for this position based on the nature of the work. 70 to 80% of your work is performed in an office environment and requires the use of office equipment and technology. you will be required to move throughout and between different office buildings and may need to complete tasks in noisy environments. you may also be required to lift and carry materials up to 10 pounds occasionally. 20 to 30% of your work will be external, at events and community organizations. this will require you to move between different locations, in varying weather conditions. you may be required to lift and carry event supplies and materials weighing up to 30 pounds occasionally.application and selection processonly on-line applications accepted. applicants for this job may be considered for other openings up to six months after the date this position is filled. applicants who meet the minimum requirements may be scheduled for an interview as well as a variety of tests to demonstrate knowledge, and skills for the position. the evaluation process may include interviews, background check, reference checks and various performance tests. employee benefitsemployees (and their families) are covered by medical, dental, vision, basic life and disability insurance. employees participate in the public employees retirement system (pers) and have the option to enroll in the throughout the calendar year. full list of all benefits and details can be found here . if you are related to or share the same living quarters of a current community transit employee, please let your qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their race, color, religion, national origin, sex, protected veteran status or disability.

this is a hybrid role and requires excellent writing, editing, story mining, and project management skills. additionally, understanding content management systems, audience segmentation, and content strategy is essential to this role.this is a hybrid role, with expectations to be onsite 2 days per week.overviewbjc healthcare is one of the largest nonprofit health care organizations in the united states, delivering services to residents primarily in the greater st. louis, southern illinois and southeast missouri regions. with net revenues of $6.3 billion and more than 30,000 employees, bjc serves patients and their families in urban, suburban and rural communities through its 14 hospitals and multiple community health locations. services include inpatient and outpatient care, primary care, community health and wellness, workplace health, home health, community mental health, rehabilitation, long-term care and hospice.bjc is the largest provider of charity care, unreimbursed care and community benefits in the state of missouri. bjc and its hospitals and health service organizations provide $785.9 million annually in community benefit. that includes $410.6 million in charity care and other financial assistance to patients to ensure medical care regardless of their ability to pay. in addition, bjc provides additional community benefits through commitments to research, emergency preparedness, regional health care safety net services, health literacy, community outreach and community health programs and regional economic development.bjc’s patients have access to the latest advances in medical science and technology through a formal affiliation between barnes-jewish hospital and st. louis children’s hospital with the renowned washington university school of medicine, which consistently ranks among the top medical schools in the country.preferred qualificationsrole purposelead communications for internal and/or external audiences that further the strategic goals and objectives of the organization. projects may include newsletters, brochures, annual reports, other collateral materials, news releases, media relations, crisis communications support, social media and web content.responsibilitiesleads and manages internal and/or external communications across multiple hsos and/or on behalf of bjc shared services for the entire organization. utilizes appropriate communication methods and tools to target information to diverse and segmented/targeted audiences. manages work of c&m team members and shared services team members.conducts and/or oversees research, interviews, writing, editing, approvals, coordination of production of collateral materials; or logistics surrounding proactive and reactive media opportunities, including crisis communications; assists hso pio in command center. reviews/edits/counsels on revisions to ensure communications deliverables align with plan objectives and hso strategic goals.analyzes communications challenges and provides recommendations to hso management, or other teams, regarding special communications needs to develop communication strategies and plans to support their business plans. provides strategic counsel on issues management and crisis response. may serve as hso spokesperson or pio.develops and implements multimedia projects/campaigns, events/media relations plans for internal and external audiences. oversees project work assigned to other team members, including shared services resources. accountable for client relations and overall results, including meeting or exceeding team and project deadlines.identifies areas where there are opportunities to improve communication efforts. creates and implements plans to effectively address deficiencies. evaluates effectiveness and proactively seeks opportunities for ongoing improvement. monitors and tracks internal and/or external communications issues and concerns, and prepares reports to support internal and/or external communications planning initiatives.minimum requirementseducationbachelor's degreeexperience10+ yearssupervisor experienceno experiencepreferred requirementseducationmaster's degreebenefits and legal statementbjc total rewardsat bjc we’re committed to providing you and your family with benefits and resources to help you manage your physical, emotional, social and financial well-being.comprehensive medical, dental, vison, life insurance, and legal services available first day of the month after hire datedisability insurance* paid for by bjcannual 4% bjc automatic retirement contribution401(k) plan with bjc matchtuition assistance available on first daybjc institute for learning and developmenthealth care and dependent care flexible
