4490476198.title: Client Technology Communications and Engagement - Associate Director

detail.desc: at ey, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.we’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. join ey and help to build a better working world.the brand, marketing and communications (bmc) function plays a critical role in achieving ey’s ambition to create long-term value as the world’s most trusted, distinctive professional services organization.through the collective power of bmc – which includes responsibility for content development, editorial and syndication through paid, owned, and earned media; webcast and live event staging; and campaign strategy, planning, and operations – we work hand in hand with ey teams to take solutions and services to market, bring our purpose of building a better working world to life, engage our people, and build the commercial value and emotional resonance of the ey brand.the opportunity client technology (ct) is at the heart of ey’s growth ambition, responsible for working with ey businesses and alliance partners to develop the global products, platforms and standards that help elevate the ey service offering, win in the market and deliver confidence to clients. as technology becomes an increasingly important driver of business transformation, enterprise resilience and client confidence, effective communication and engagement are critical to realizing the value that ct delivers.as a communications and engagement lead within the ct bmc team, you will lead the global communications, engagement and adoption strategy to shape how technologists in ey understand, trust and adopt the platforms, standards and capabilities that ct provides. you will be responsible for translating complex technology and transformation priorities into clear, compelling narratives that inspire action, drive behavior change and strengthen confidence in ct across the organization.this is a senior, high-impact role at the heart of ey's ai-first transformation. acting as a trusted advisor to ct leadership, including the ct operating committee and the global vice chair – client technology, you will shape executive communications, influence strategic decisions, and help ensure ct communicates with clarity, consistency and confidence at the moments that matter most.you will also play a critical role in strengthening ct's position as one of ey's most compelling client zero stories, helping technologists and client-serving teams understand how ey applies its own technology capabilities to create business value and build confidence with clients.this role requires a strategic communications leader who thrives in a fast-paced, complex, global environment and can influence senior stakeholders, navigate ambiguity, and drive measurable business outcomes through communications, engagement and adoption strategies.your key responsibilities strategic communications and engagement leadership: own and evolve the global communications, engagement and adoption strategy for ey global standards, our ey fabric technology platform and operations and support capabilities, to strengthen the security and scalability of ey technology and deliver confidence to help ey client servers win in the market.executive advisory and leadership communications: act as a trusted communications advisor to ct senior leadership, including members of the ct operating committee and the global vice chair – client technology. provide strategic counsel on executive positioning, organizational change, transformation initiatives, leadership engagement and complex communications challenges. serve as deputy to the ct bmc leader on communications and engagement activities.global narrative, positioning and message architecture: lead the development of global positioning, messaging and narrative frameworks for ct's capabilities, standards, platforms and strategic initiatives, working with g&i bmc leads, including the tech marketing lead and platform marketing lead, to ensure alignment with broader technology messaging. partner closely with global, region and service line bmc teams and stakeholders to ensure consistent, audience-centric communications and alignment across ey.adoption and change communications: design and execute engagement strategies that accelerate adoption of ct standards, platforms and strategic capabilities. apply change management and behavior change principles to help drive secure, scalable and consistent technology development practices across the global ey technologist community.transformation campaign leadership: lead integrated communications for ct's most significant transformation priorities and emerging technology capabilities. set strategic direction for complex global campaigns, balancing long-term engagement objectives with rapid-response support for high-visibility business, technology and leadership moments.knowledge sharing: facilitate knowledge sharing across the ey technologist community that promote the skillsets, mindsets and toolsets required to be a technologist of the future. propose original channels and communications that resonate with target audiences, and reflect ct’s position as ai-first technology experts within ey.insight, measurement and performance optimization: conduct adoption analysis and audience segmentation to identify gaps and inform internal marketing strategies and campaigns. establish and lead the ct bmc measurement framework, defining success metrics that demonstrate business impact and communication effectiveness. leverage audience insights, adoption analytics and performance data to optimize strategy, improve engagement and guide investment decisions.operating model and team leadership: lead and develop the ct content delivery team, building a high-performing communications capability that supports ct's global objectives. define and continuously improve communication processes, governance, templates, channels and measurement practices, embedding a scalable and data-driven approach across ct bmc.skills and attributes for successexecutive presence and strategic influence: demonstrated experience advising and influencing senior leaders within large, highly matrixed global organizations. ability to build credibility quickly, challenge constructively and operate as a trusted advisor at executive level.strategic communications leadership: extensive experience developing enterprise-wide communications strategies that support transformation, adoption and business change. proven ability to align communication activity to measurable organizational outcomes.global stakeholder management: exceptional ability to build relationships, navigate complexity and influence diverse stakeholder groups across functions, geographies and leadership levels.storytelling and communication excellence: outstanding storytelling, editorial and executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technology and transformation concepts into compelling narratives tailored to diverse audiences. exceptional attentional to detail.change and adoption expertise: strong understanding of change communications, engagement strategies and behavior change principles, with experience driving adoption and engagement at scale.data-driven decision making: strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities, with the ability to derive actionable insights from audience, engagement and adoption data and translate them into communications strategies that deliver measurable impact.digital and ai fluency: strong understanding of emerging technologies, digital channels, ai enabled communications and innovative engagement approaches. demonstrated ability to leverage technology to improve reach, relevance, efficiency and impact.leadership and team development: experience leading high-performing teams, setting strategic direction, building capability and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and collaboration.global experience: extensive experience leading and working with global, cross-border communications initiatives, successfully managing multiple complex programmes and stakeholders across geographies, leveraging a strong network.what we look forwe’re looking for a senior communications professional who embraces technology, brings curiosity and energy, and works collaboratively with leaders and teams to deliver meaningful engagement.what we offer youthe compensation ranges below are provided in order to comply with united states pay transparency laws. other geographies will follow their local salary guidelines, which may not be a direct conversion of published us salary ranges. at ey, we harness our collective strength to empower you to shape your future with confidence through professional growth, personal fulfillment and an inclusive culture. learn more at ey.com/us/careers.we offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to the business. the base salary range for this job is:new york city, boston, and washington dc metro areas, washington state, and southern california offices – $154,300 to $277,700bay area california offices – $160,700 to $289,300all other offices locations in the us, including sacramento – $128,600 to $254,600individual salaries within these ranges are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge, skills and geography. in addition, our total rewards package includes medical and dental coverage, pension and 401(k) plans, and a wide range of paid time off options.under our flexible vacation policy, you’ll decide how much vacation time you need based on your own personal circumstances. you’ll also be granted time off for designated ey paid holidays, winter/summer breaks, personal/family care, and other leaves of absence when needed to support your physical, financial, and emotional well-being.are you ready to shape your future with confidence? apply today. to make the most of your application experience, please limit yourself to two applications within a six-month period.ey accepts applications for this position on an on-going basis.for those living in california, please click here for additional information.at ey, our values set the foundation for how we work and the behaviors we expect of our people. any misrepresentation or falsification of information or lack of integrity at any point in the recruiting process may result in withdrawal of your candidacy, revocation of an offer or immediate termination of employment.ey | building a better working worldey is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.enabled by data, ai and advanced technology, ey teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.ey teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, ey teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.all in to shape the future with confidence.ey to protect and improve cisco's reputation through innovative and thought-provoking storytelling, execution excellence and transparency. the pr team is responsible for leading cisco's corporate and technology pr programs, as well as crafting and delivering clear and compelling narratives that grab the attention of media and influencers.your impactas a pr manager for cisco’s networking portfolio, you will shape the narrative around cisco’s networking reinvention in the ai era. you’ll operate at the center of our business, translating product innovations into high-impact stories that resonate with enterprise leaders and practitioner audiences, including network architects, engineers, and it/ot teams. this role represents an opportunity to tell high-impact stories and connect the dots between networking infrastructure and customer outcomes that define the ai era.in this role, you will own communications programs within our campus & branch and industrial networking portfolio, acting as a trusted advisor to business leadership. you’ll lead product announcements, work with our customers and partners to tell impactful stories, draft compelling messaging and other high-impact communications content, and work with media and influencers to advance cisco’s narrative around cisco’s enterprise connectivity platform. you’ll bridge the gap between technical product capabilities and the broader market shifts, ensuring cisco’s networking story is consistent, compelling, and ahead of the competitive curve.key responsibilitiesstorytelling & discovery: lead the development of comprehensive storytelling strategies that unify product launches, customer success stories, and thought leadership. you will proactively identify market opportunities to position cisco’s networking portfolio as the backbone of the ai era. working with product and engineering teams, customers, and practitioners, you’ll translate technical roadmaps, architectures, workflows, and operational trade-offs into credible stories that connect to customer outcomes for business leaders and practitioner audiences. cross-functional collaboration & stakeholder management: serve as the primary communications partner to senior networking leadership, providing strategic counsel on messaging, reputation, and global alignment. you will manage competing priorities across a matrixed environment, ensuring that pr goals are integrated with business, marketing, and analyst relations objectives. media relations: nurture high-level relationships with key technology and business media to drive consistent, high-impact coverage. serve as a trusted advisor to our spokespeople, coaching them on narrative delivery and ensuring our messaging remains sharp, influential, and aligned with market trends. strategic counsel: serve as a trusted strategic advisor to product, product marketing, and executive leadership. bring external market perspective (competitive moves, media sentiment, industry trends) to internal decision-making. campaign management: own end-to-end campaign execution for launches and strategic initiatives—from strategy through measurement. manage timelines, agency relationships, and multi-channel delivery, leveraging ai tools and automation to accelerate workflows without sacrificing editorial rigor. lead coordination with other communications functions, including analyst relations, employee communications and digital communications. minimum qualifications8+ years of experience in public relations, with a proven track record in enterprise technology communications. demonstrated technical fluency in enterprise networking and ai, with the ability to engage credibly on areas such as campus and branch, wireless, routing and switching, security, and industrial networking. proven ability to reach and earn trust with practitioner audiences through relevant technology media, technical content, customer stories, events, or practitioner communities. demonstrated experience to act as a strategic advisor to senior leadership, influencing decision-making through market intelligence and communication strategy. exceptional writing and editorial skills; ability to craft compelling bylines, reports, and messaging frameworks that capture market attention. track record of building relationships with media and influencers; demonstrated ability to secure coverage in relevant publications. strong cross-functional collaboration skills—proven ability to work effectively with product, marketing and executive teams; skilled at managing up, across, and down in matrixed environments. self-starter mentality—bias toward discovery and action; ability to identify storytelling opportunities and refine narrative direction with minimal direction. demonstrated ability to navigate cross-functional tensions and resolve complex communication challenges within a large, matrixed organization. preferred qualificationsproven experience in managing agency relationships and driving cross-functional alignment across marketing, analyst relations, and employee communications. deep familiarity with the networking landscape, including trends like intent-based networking, security, and ai-powered operations. strong use of ai in day-to-day operations with a hunger to always be learning more; early-adopter mentality. why cisco?at cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the ai era – and beyond. we’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. these solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. we work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.we are cisco, and our priorities established by the pastors and session. the production team may include staff members, interns, contractors, and volunteers; its composition may evolve according to ministry needs and available resources.specific duties and responsibilities1. planning and visiona. develop and implement a church-wide communications strategy aligned with spc's mission, congregational life, and the messaging, and propose integrated strategies in support of ministry goals.c. establish and maintain communications calendars, submission processes, editorial standards, brand standards, and approval workflows.d. assess communication practices, technologies, production processes, and results; recommend improvements and lead implementation of approved changes.2. production team leadershipa. serve leaders so that production serves the purpose and flow of each service or event.g. maintain quality-control practices and recommend production equipment, software, training, and budget priorities.3. communications productiona. personally plan, write, design, prepare, publish, and distribute much of the church's routine communication, including the weekly e-mail, sunday announcements, publications, promotional materials, signage, mailings, and pastoral or ministry communications.b. develop faithful, engaging, and informative messaging for internal and external audiences, with top-flight writing, editing, and graphic-design quality.c. create unified visual themes for events, programs, campaigns, publications, and annual projects while maintaining spc brand standards and producing materials that are legible and engaging across generations.d. collaborate with staff and production team personnel on video and multimedia content and manage print and publication processes through production and distribution.e. coordinate publicity, advertising, press releases, and relationships with external media, and maintain appropriate copyright, trademark, licensing, permission, attribution, and usage practices.4. digital communicationsa. direct and maintain the church's online presence, including website content and function, social media, e-mail priorities.d. maintain organized files, calendars, procedures, credentials, and documentation so essential work can continue during absences and transitions.e. coordinate the content and visual consistency of building signage and other public-facing materials to support a welcoming environment for guests.f. coordinate with operations regarding shared technology, equipment, and systems related to communications and production.g. perform other duties consistent with the purpose and leadership level of the position as assigned.personal attributesthe communications director must be make kai impossible for builders to ignore.what would you make if your job was to take over the builder internet for the day?we’re looking for a hands-on maker with serious video craft, sharp social instincts and the ambition to create breakout moments. someone who sees the hook, makes the thing and gets it in front of people. you want real views, real conversation and work developers remember when they build their next feature.kai is k-id’s self-serve console and sdk for age- and jurisdiction-adaptive access and consent. builders declare what their product does; kai configures the underlying compliance development kit (cdk). their app enforces the returned permissions. the question becomes: “what can this person do in my product, and what needs to happen first?”your job is to make that story travel.what you’ll domake the work yourself. research, interview, write, record, edit, package and publish. turn builder problems into screen-recorded demos, short videos, native posts and useful explainers. own the hook, pacing, sound, captions, readable software screens, titles and thumbnails. know when a simple screen recording is the strongest choice. create breakout moments. build coordinated launches around a supported demo, a useful insight or a compelling builder story. bring together a standout video or demo, platform-native edits, founder participation and credible distribution partners. try to make kai the thing builders are sharing today, then learn and launch again. develop founder voices. interview our founders for their strongest ideas. make distinct posts, videos and conversations that sound like them. keep approvals lightweight and help them participate when builders respond. give people a reason to follow their thinking, beyond reposting the company account. build precise creator collaborations. find creators and practitioners who ship software and reach the right builders. develop joint demos, interviews and launch assets. carry the production work that makes collaboration easy. own the brief, delivery, disclosure and distribution, choosing credible audience overlap over follower count or mass outreach. tell the technical story accurately. use kai, follow a supported integration with technical help and talk to builders about their decisions. work with product and engineering to validate demonstrations. explain age signals, consent and access permissions clearly. keep limitations honest: kai is not compliance certification or a guarantee of platform approval. improve through evidence. choose a few formats you can make exceptionally well. experiment with hooks, packaging and distribution; study what traveled and why. participate usefully in builder communities. report genuine reach and observable product outcomes separately, distinguish organic from paid delivery and reject manufactured engagement. what you bringfinished video and social work that shows your taste, editing ability and understanding of how each platform works. evidence you can earn attention: a launch, a cold-start channel, a breakout post or a creator collaboration you helped make happen. technical curiosity and the ability to make a software demo understandable without making unsupported claims. strong interviewing and writing instincts, with the range to preserve someone else’s voice. the judgment to move quickly, finish work independently and learn from an experiment that missed. we care about what you can make and explain. famous logos and a large personal following won’t substitute for craft. tools and ai can speed up production; your taste and judgment still decide what ships.what success looks likemore genuine views and impressions. stronger sharing. growing social audiences. founder ideas reaching new circles. launch moments that break beyond the people who already know us.builder adoption matters too: people understand kai, visit, sign up, integrate and keep using it where those outcomes can be observed. a big attention win matters before it becomes revenue. a large view count does not prove product use. we want both reported honestly.kai firstyou’ll report to mike mongeau, head of product, and work with product, design and engineering. you own media, social execution, founder programming and selected creator collaborations; product decisions and compliance sign-off stay with their owners.once a kai approach works, we may reuse the production and launch kit for one bounded ventures product, with an explicit priority and capacity decision, including what pauses. you won’t be running every venture at once.how to applyinclude a small portfolio of finished videos and social work you personally made. tell us exactly what you did, the audience you were trying to reach, the observed results and their time window. include one experiment that failed and what you learned. be ready to walk through your source files and decisions.finalists may be invited to a three-hour take-home exercise, with no live posting or outreach.if you’d rather make the thing than present the plan, we’d like to see your work.applicants privacy policy

and leadership communications. support communications related to organizational changes, business initiatives, employee programs and company events. assist with developing messaging and communications plans in collaboration with business leaders and subject matter experts. support town halls, employee meetings and engagement initiatives by creating presentations and supporting communications materials, analyzing survey results and preparing post-meeting summaries. content developmentwrite, edit and proofread content for a variety of audiences and channels. translate complex or technical information into clear, concise and engaging messages. ensure consistency of voice, tone and messaging across external and internal communications. develop communications plans, messaging frameworks, presentations and other materials that support business priorities. project management & collaborationmanage communications projects from strategy and planning through execution. build strong relationships with leaders and stakeholders across the organization. manage multiple projects and competing priorities while meeting deadlines. manage day-to-day relationships with external communications agencies and other partners as needed. qualificationsqualificationsthe ideal candidate should possess the following:bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, communications. experience developing media statements, press releases, talking points, holding statements and other external communications materials. experience managing or coordinating responses to savant is seeking an experienced, proactive, and highly organized public relations manager to help build, maintain, and support the firm's reputation with the external audiences most central to its growth. those audiences include prospective acquisition partners, the wealth management industry, regulators, and consumers. earned media and published thought leadership are the primary vehicles this role uses to reach them. this role manages savant's day-to-day external public relations activity. responsibilities span media relations, news release development, ghostwritten executive thought leadership, awards and recognition programs, spokesperson preparation, and crisis communication readiness. working closely with marketing leadership, savant's public relations agency, executive leaders, and subject matter experts across the firm, the public relations manager will help identify story opportunities, coordinate responses to media inquiries, and work with savant’s pr agency, internal communications leader, and marketing leadership to reach savant's target audiences.the ideal candidate writes exceptionally well in other people's voices, understands how newsrooms operate, and manages competing deadlines without sacrificing accuracy. this individual brings ideas forward, works comfortably with senior leaders and reporters alike, and exercises sound judgment in a regulated industry.duties and responsibilitiesmedia relations and external public relationssupports the development and execution of savant's external public relations strategy, consistent with the firm's brand and business objectives. supports leadership’s day-to-day contact with savant's public relations agency, helping coordinate news release development and distribution, proactive pitching, and interview requests. builds and maintains working relationships with reporters, editors, and producers at the outlets that reach savant's target audiences. maintains a forward-looking editorial calendar of story opportunities, firm announcements, and industry news hooks. responds to inbound media inquiries promptly and route them to the appropriate spokesperson. tracks, logs, and reports media coverage, and shares results with marketing leadership and firm stakeholders. works with new savant partners and the m&a team to assess media relationships, spokesperson roles, and past media activity to determine public relations opportunities. writing, ghostwriting, and thought leadershipwrites news releases, media pitches (as needed), key messages, talking points, and executive quotes using ap style. develops editorial calendar, coordinates contributions, and writes savant talk, savant’s quarterly client newsletter. ghostwrites bylined articles, commentary, and other thought leadership material on behalf of savant leaders and subject matter experts. interviews subject matter experts to capture their expertise and translate it into clear, jargon-free content for external audiences. helps place bylined content with trade and consumer publications, then track and report placements. maintains boilerplate language, fact sheets, executive biographies, and the firm's online newsroom. partners with the content team to repurpose earned media and bylined articles across the website, social media, and other marketing channels. prepares announcement materials and local market media outreach that support savant's merger and acquisition activity and its visibility with prospective acquisition partners. submits all external materials for compliance review and maintain the required records. spokesperson preparation and media trainingprepares briefing documents, background research, key messages, and anticipated questions for savant spokespersons ahead of interviews. helps coach spokespersons on messaging and delivery and debrief with them after interviews and appearances. coordinates regular media training for executives and advisors. maintains a roster of approved spokespersons and their areas of expertise. awards and recognitionmaintains a calendar of award and recognition opportunities, including deadlines, criteria, and submission requirements. partners with the business intelligence team and advisory leadership to gather supporting data and write compelling entries. tracks results and promote wins across earned, owned, and internal channels. crisis communicationmaintains and update savant's crisis communication plan, contact trees, and holding statements. monitors for emerging issues and alert leadership promptly. drafts response messaging and coordinates with legal, compliance, and executive leadership during an active issue. coordinates periodic crisis readiness exercises with key stakeholders. additional responsibilitiesrecommends vendors, tools, and budget allocations that support savant's external communication goals. supports content development and writing projects as needed. collaborates effectively with marketing, compliance, internal communication, and executive stakeholders. occasionally travels to conferences, firm events, and other content-gathering opportunities. represents savant in a positive and professional manner. adheres to savant's policies, procedures, and core values. performs additional duties may be assigned as needed to support business and role needs. as the firm and role evolve, responsibilities may be refined or adjusted to meet business needs, consistent with the overall purpose and scope of the role. qualificationsthis role typically requires the following:excellent writing, editing, and proofreading skills, with a strong command of ap style. demonstrated ability to write in another person's voice. working knowledge of media operations, deadlines, and what makes a story newsworthy. exceptional project management and organizational abilities. strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy. ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and stakeholders simultaneously. ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment with minimal supervision. strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build rapport quickly with reporters and internal experts. comfort working directly with executive leaders and subject matter experts. discretion in handling confidential and market-sensitive information. proficiency with media sourcing and monitoring platforms, such as qwoted, and with content management systems. a portfolio of published writing samples is required. educationbachelor's degree in journalism, communications, public relations, marketing, or a related field. experience5-7 years of public relations, corporate communication, or journalism experience. demonstrated experience pitching and placing stories with trade or consumer media. demonstrated experience ghostwriting bylined articles or commentary for executives or subject matter experts. experience preparing and supporting executive spokespersons. designations / certificationsaccreditation in public relations (apr) from the public relations society of america is desirable but not required.preferred qualificationsexperience in financial services, wealth management, or another regulated industry. public relations agency experience. experience with qwoted or similar media sourcing and monitoring platforms. experience supporting merger and acquisition announcements or other corporate news. experience supporting executive thought leadership initiatives. familiarity with financial and investment concepts. working knowledge of design or content management tools such as adobe indesign. our total rewardsat savant, we invest in our people—supporting both their well-being and long-term growth. we take a market-based approach to compensation. the expected base salary range for this role is $90,000-120,000. actual compensation is determined on an individual basis and considers factors such as relevant experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, and market conditions. this role may also be eligible for additional incentive compensation based on responsibilities and performance.core benefits (effective day one)medical, dental, and vision coverage with multiple plan options health savings account (hsa) or flexible spending account (fsa) company-paid life insurance, ad&d, and disability coverage financial & long-term rewards401(k) with company match (roth and traditional options) team-based incentive opportunities and recognition program time away & flexibilitygenerous paid time off, plus at least 10 paid holidays annual “savantiversary” day summer hours (shorter work weeks during the summer) parental leave, personal leave, and other life-event support well-being & everyday perksemployee assistance program (eap) wellness reimbursements (e.g., gym memberships) flexible “dress for your day” approach we’re happy to share more details about our benefits and total rewards during the hiring process.take your career to new heights, apply today!all applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the u.s. we are unable to sponsor or title: media relations manageroffice/department: marketing and communicationsdescription: the grove city college is seeking a skilled and strategic media relations manager to enhance the institution’s visibility, credibility, and reputation through proactive media engagement and earned media coverage. this individual will serve as the primary liaison between the college and external media outlets, building strong relationships with journalists, editors, producers, and other media professionals while identifying opportunities to showcase the college’s faculty, students, leadership, programs, and institutional achievements.the successful candidate will develop and implement comprehensive media relations strategies aligned with the college’s strategic priorities and institutional goals. responsibilities include identifying and pitching compelling stories, securing positive media coverage, responding to media inquiries, coordinating interviews, and preparing press releases, media advisories, official statements, talking points, and other communications materials. the position will work closely with college leadership, faculty, administrators, and subject-matter experts to experience for our customers. we work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company’s success. as a content strategy lead within pnc's content center of excellence organization, you will be based in pittsburgh, pa or new york, new york.additional locations within the pnc footprint may be considered.pnc’s content center of excellence (coe) is building out its founding leadership team, and our content strategy lead will define the strategy behind what we create.this senior role sits at the intersection of audience intelligence, content strategy, marketing, communications, and digital experience. the content strategy lead will build a deep understanding of pnc’s priority audiences, using quantitative and qualitative research, behavioral data, search and social insights, competitive intelligence, and direct audience research to understand what matters to them, what questions they have, where pnc can credibly add value, and what moves them to act.this is a role meant for a builder. the mandate goes well beyond developing individual content strategies or editorial calendars or content design systems. the content strategy lead will create the planning and measurement system for the coe: audience definitions and insights, messaging frameworks, content priorities, channel and distribution strategies, goals and kpis, measurement frameworks, and planning processes that connect business priorities to the work teams produce every day.great content has limited value if the right audience never encounters it. this leader will identify and build the organic and owned distribution levers that allow pnc content to travel further across pnc.com, search, social, email, crm, executive channels, partner platforms, and other audience touchpoints.reporting to the head of content, this role partners across creative, editorial, digital experience, analytics, research, brand marketing, paid media, and business leaders to develop and execute an integrated content strategy aligned with audience needs and business priorities. the ideal candidate combines audience-centric thinking, strategic planning, data-driven decision making, and strong execution skills to determine what content will have the greatest impact, who it should reach, and how success will be measured.key responsibilitiesaudience strategy & intelligence: define priority audiences, build audience frameworks, uncover customer insights, and leverage research, behavioral data, and market intelligence to inform strategy.content strategy, messaging & editorial planning: develop enterprise content strategies, create messaging frameworks and narratives, establish editorial priorities, and lead content planning across channels.distribution & audience growth: build distribution strategies, optimize content across platforms, expand audience reach and engagement, and continuous improvement through testing and optimization.research & insights: lead audience, competitive, and market research efforts; identify emerging trends; and translate findings into actionable strategic recommendations.cross-functional leadership & operating model: partner with creative, editorial, digital, analytics, and business stakeholders to create planning processes, governance frameworks, and scalable operating models.content creation & production: shape how content is conceived, designed, and produced across the enterprise, integrating content marketing and content design capabilities to turn audience and business needs into effective content experiences.ai-enabled content strategy: apply ai to audience research, content planning, analysis, and optimization while ensuring responsible, compliant, and effective use of emerging technologies.pnc is an in-office company that fosters a supportive culture where employees can thrive and achieve balance. we encourage the director of media relations serves as a key partner in sharing the cathedral’s voice, mission, and public presence with audiences across the country. this role leads the cathedral’s media engagement and plays a central part in shaping written content that supports institutional priorities.  the director provides writing and editorial support for a wide range of platforms, including cathedral age (the cathedral’s magazine), cathedral connects blog, crossroads podcast, statements, remarks, and national moments requiring timely reflection. the role also serves as the primary point of contact for all media inquiries, coordinating responses, preparing leadership for interviews, and supporting proactive earned media efforts that highlight cathedral worship, programs, and events. in partnership with senior leadership and the cathedral’s strategic communications firm, the director supports crisis communications and contributes to coordinated messaging during urgent or sensitive situations. the position represents the cathedral in interactions with reporters, partner organizations, and the broader public, helping to strengthen relationships and expand awareness of the cathedral’s work and witness. this is a collaborative, forward-facing role that requires strong judgment, exceptional writing skills, sensitivity to tone, and the ability to navigate both routine and high-profile communications with care and professionalism.  duties and responsibilities: media relations and public affairs primary point of contact for media serve as the cathedral’s main point of contact for incoming media inquiries.  coordinate media visits to the cathedral, including set-up, security coordination, and on-site support. prepare cathedral leaders and subject matter experts for interviews. this may include developing talking points, briefing materials, practice questions, and suggested framing. build and maintain positive relationships with reporters, editors, producers, and partner institutions. serve as a media spokesperson when appropriate. proactive earned media strategy develop and support proactive media engagement that increases public awareness of cathedral programs, services, and institutional priorities. this includes but is not limited to: identifying story opportunities that align with mission and have news value pitching stories to targeted reporters and outlets coordinating with marketing and communications staff to shape media calendars and messaging highlighting seasonal priorities such as christmas, easter, concerts, and public programs working with departments to surface events or initiatives that have strong public interest potential crisis communications and emergency response support crisis communications planning and response to help ensure consistent communication during urgent or sensitive situations. monitoring and analysis monitor media coverage and identify themes, opportunities, and risks.  public ambassador for the cathedral represent the cathedral in public and professional settings.  writing and editorial leadership principal writer for cathedral communications develop clear and compelling written materials for the cathedral as a whole, including statements, reflections, speeches, remarks, website content, and other pieces that support institutional priorities. including but not limited to: executive editor for cathedral age oversee editorial planning and content development for cathedral age in partnership with marketing and communications staff.  blog and feature writing write and edit stories for cathedral blogs, newsletters, and related platforms. highlight cathedral life, worship, programs, national moments, and community impact.  podcast content development shape and support podcast content, including scripts, outlines, and narrative structure.  national moments and rapid response writing draft timely reflections and statements for moments of national importance. provide rapid response writing so that public messages are thoughtful, relevant, and coordinated. editorial quality and institutional alignment serve as an editorial partner across departments as needed. help ensure that cathedral-wide communications are clear, consistent, and reflective of cathedral values.  perform other duties as assigned.   minimum qualifications: bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, english, or a related field at least seven years of experience in media relations, public affairs, journalism, strategic communications, or a related discipline demonstrated experience responding to media inquiries and working directly with reporters proven ability to write quickly, clearly, and in multiple voices for a range of platforms, including statements, articles, speeches, and digital content  preferred qualifications: previous experience in a communications or media role within a complex nonprofit, faith-based institution, cultural organization, or mission-driven entity experience managing or supporting editorial processes for publications or institutional communications demonstrated success in proactive media outreach, including pitching stories and securing earned media placements strong understanding of digital communications strategy, analytics, and audience engagement  abilities, knowledge, and skills: intellectually curious empathetic and able to navigate sensitive topics with care strategic thinker who can balance long-term planning with day-to-day execution excellent copywriting and editing skills, with the ability to write clearly in the cathedral’s tone and voice ability to assess news value, identify story opportunities, and support proactive earned media efforts strong verbal and written communication skills for a wide range of audiences strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving abilities ability to work with confidential information and maintain discretion   working conditions: this position requires work during regular business hours. at times, some work on weekends and outside of regular business hours may be required. this position is eligible for a hybrid model of work, requiring at least 3 days/week in the office. the position requires prolonged sitting, standing, walking, reaching, twisting, turning, kneeling, bending, and stooping in the performance of daily activities. the position also requires grasping, repetitive hand movement, and fine coordination in preparing reports using a computer keyboard. the position also requires near and far vision for reading and preparing written reports and other required documents. acute hearing is also required when providing phone assistance. the need to lift, drag, push, and pull files, reports and other materials weighing up to 25 pounds is also required.   washington national cathedral is an equal opportunity employer and strives to create a more diverse and inclusive atmosphere for all. applicants will not be discriminated against because of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.  we support an inclusive workplace where associates excel based on personal merit, qualifications, experience, ability, and job performance.  washington national cathedral seeks individuals who are committed to our mission. we appreciate interest from those who will contribute to an atmosphere in which diversity is valued and supported. ***submission requirements***to submit your application, please fill out the online application, submit your resume/cv, a cover letter, and any portfolio materials that may help us understand your writing style.salary is $90,000 - $95,000 commensurate to experience

4492012992.title: Director, Advocacy and Member Communications
4492012992.company: The Hospital and Healthsystem Association of Pennsylvania

detail.desc: the hospital and healthsystem association of pennsylvania (hap) is seeking candidates for director, advocacy & member communications. this role is a key contributor to the association’s proactive and reactive communications to external audiences and works collaboratively across departments to develop messages and materials that advance the association’s mission, goals, and priorities. in addition, this position drives the development and execution of effective, engaging, multi-channel communications that inform members, strengthen stakeholder engagement, and advance organizational objectives.candidates for consideration must have a bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations or a related field with five or more years of professional experience in content development, marketing, or related field. in addition, the candidate must demonstrate the ability to translate complex issues, public policy topics, and/or technical information into clear, engaging content for diverse audiences. experience within healthcare, a hospital, association, or agency environment is preferred.hap offers a generous benefit package (medical, dental, vision, life, ad&d, ltd, eap, tuition reimbursement, fsa, health savings accounts, 401(k) with immediate vesting, wellness programs, professional development, travel accident, vacation, sick, discount programs, work-life balance, flexibility) and competitive pay. this is a hybrid position.eeo employer f/m/veterans/disabled are encouraged to apply.to apply, please send your resume to kmccoy@haponline.org or mail to the hospital and healthsystem association of pennsylvania, attn: kim mccoy, 30 north third street, suite 600, harrisburg, pa 17101.

descriptionabout asphalt green asphalt green is a nonprofit organization that transforms lives and builds community through sports, fitness, and play for all.each year, asphalt green serves thousands of new yorkers through sports, aquatics, fitness, camps, and community programs that promote health, personal growth, and lifelong participation in physical activity. across three campuses and numerous community partnerships, asphalt green is committed to providing high-quality programs that are inclusive, accessible, and rooted in excellence.asphalt green believes that access to movement, sport, and wellness can change lives. our work helps young people develop confidence, resilience, leadership skills, and healthy habits that extend far beyond the playing field.about the role the director of communications leads asphalt green's communications function and serves as the strategic steward of the organization's voice, messaging, and reputation. reporting to the chief marketing officer, this role develops and executes integrated communications strategies that elevate brand awareness, strengthen community engagement, support fundraising and programmatic objectives, and ensure consistent storytelling across all channels.the director oversees internal and external communications systems, content strategy, executive communications, and organizational messaging. this leader partners closely with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to translate organizational priorities into compelling communications that advance asphalt green's mission and business goals.portfolio scope leads communications strategy for an organization operating across 3 campuses and dozens of community-based locations throughout all five boroughs of new york city.oversees communications supporting 1m+ annual visits, 6,500+ members, and 800+ employees.supports an organization investing $17m+ annually in free and subsidized programming.leads enterprise communications across all organizational business lines, locations, and stakeholder groups.oversees organizational messaging, executive communications, institutional thought leadership, internal communications, member communications, and retention communications.supports publication of 6+ original thought leadership pieces annually.supports 8+ executive and staff speaking engagements annually.supports a targeted 20% year-over-year increase in media visibility and thought leadership exposure.advances thought leadership across 5 strategic pillars: program innovation, community impact, organizational voice & advocacy, staff expertise & development, and research & learning.supervises 1 direct report.why this role matters communications is responsible for defining and managing asphalt green's voice, narrative, and institutional story. it ensures consistency across all organizational communications while translating program outcomes, community impact, staff expertise, and organizational priorities into compelling narratives that strengthen engagement and retention. the function serves as the steward of asphalt green's institutional thought leadership strategy, elevating executive voices, showcasing staff expertise, producing strategic content, and helping position the organization as a recognized leader in sports, fitness, play, aquatics, youth development, inclusion, and public health. communications also supports internal alignment, executive communications, member and participant retention, and the storytelling necessary to demonstrate the organization's impact, innovation, and expertise.working closely with leadership across programs, development, customer experience, ag impact, operations, communications, and executive leadership, the senior director ensures organizational priorities are translated into clear, audience-centered communications that advance business and mission objectives.what you’ll do strategic communications leadershipdevelop and execute a comprehensive communications strategy aligned with asphalt green's organizational goals and strategic priorities.serve as the primary steward of the asphalt green brand voice, ensuring consistency in internal and external messaging across all channels.help position asphalt green as a thought leader in sports, fitness, recreation, public health, and youth development.advise executive and senior leadership on communications opportunities, challenges, and reputational considerations.establish communications goals, metrics, and reporting frameworks to evaluate effectiveness and impact.brand & content strategylead the creation and execution of integrated content strategies that engage key audiences, including members, participants, donors, partners, employees, and the broader community.oversee editorial planning and content development across web, email, social media, publications, marketing collateral, and executive communications.ensure messaging effectively communicates asphalt green's mission, programs, impact, and value proposition.develop and manage publication strategy of research-driven impact reports, white papers, and other thought leadership content.internal communicationsdevelop and lead internal communications strategies that strengthen employee engagement, organizational alignment, and understanding of asphalt green’s priorities.partner with human resources and executive leadership on organizational announcements, leadership communications, and change management initiatives.establish communication standards and channels that support timely, transparent, and consistent information-sharing across departments and locations.member & operational communicationsoversee enterprise communications to members, participants, families, and community stakeholders.establish standardized systems for timely, accurate, and accessible operational communications, including facility updates, program and schedule changes, safety notifications, policy updates, and service announcements.lead communications planning and response during unforeseen incidents, emergencies, service disruptions, and sensitive operational situations, in coordination with the crisis response team, operations, customer experience, and executive leadership.team leadership & operationslead, coach, and develop communications staff, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.establish workflows, editorial processes, and project management systems that enable high-quality execution and scalability.manage communications budgets, vendor relationships, agencies, freelancers, and external partners as needed.oversee communications calendars and priorities across multiple stakeholders and business functions.what success looks like within your first 12–18 months, you will:establish a clear, organization-wide communications strategy that supports asphalt green's strategic objectives.strengthen brand consistency and messaging across all communication channels.increase visibility and awareness through thought leadership opportunities.improve communication effectiveness through measurable engagement and performance metrics.build strong partnerships across departments, serving as a trusted advisor to organizational leaders.develop a high-performing communications function capable of supporting asphalt green's continued growth and impact.who you’ll work with this role reports to the chief marketing officer and collaborates closely with the executive leadership team,development, programs, operations, human resources, marketing, external engagement, and externalpartners, including media outlets, agencies, and community stakeholders.qualificationsrequired qualifications you’ll need:bachelor's degree in communications, public relations, journalism, marketing, english, or a related field.8+ years of progressive communications or strategic communications experience.3+ years of people management experience, including coaching and developing team members.demonstrated success leading integrated communications strategies for complex organizations.exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills across multiple formats and audiences.strong project management, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.preferred qualifications it would be helpful if you also have:experience within nonprofit, education, youth development, recreation, health and wellness, or mission-driven organizations.experience supporting executive communications and organizational change initiatives.familiarity with crisis communications planning and management.experience overseeing agencies, consultants, and external partners.strong understanding of digital communications channels, analytics, and content performance measurementschedule and work environment this is a full-time, hybrid-eligible position based at asphalt green’s upper east side headquarters. the typical schedule is monday through friday, approximately 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m., with an expectation of working onsite three to four days per week and opportunities for remote work one to two days per week.as a senior communications leader supporting multiple campuses, programs, and stakeholder groups, occasional flexibility outside of standard business hours may be required to support organizational priorities, events, urgent communications, or time-sensitive situations.physical requirements this role may require the ability to:stand, walk, sit, bend, or move for extended periods.lift, carry, push, or pull up to [insert weight].work in [pool, gym, office, outdoor, event, or facility] environments.use equipment, supplies, or technology related to the role.perform other physical tasks required for safe and effective job performance.reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.

detail.desc: job title: manager, rare diseases franchise global communicationslocation: cambridge, maabout the jobready to push the limits of what’s possible? join sanofi’s global rare diseases communications team and you can play a vital part in elevating our leadership in novel first-in-class and best-in-class medicines within rare diseases while helping to make an impact on patients around the world.as manager, rare diseases franchise global communications, you will play an important role in supporting product communications across rare diseases, including both marketed and investigational products, with a focus on lysosomal storage disorders and support for select rare blood disorders as needed. working closely with the global head of rare diseases communications and cross-functional partners, you will help develop and execute communications for product, data and regulatory milestones, congresses, and unbranded disease education and awareness initiatives.this manager will sit within the global rare diseases communications team, which is responsible for the strategy and execution of global communications activities for marketed products and investigational programs across sanofi’s rare diseases portfolio. the manager will independently manage defined communications workstreams, contribute strategic recommendations and provide day-to-day support to cross-functional partners under the direction of the global head of rare diseases communications. the position will be based in cambridge, massachusetts.we are an innovative global healthcare company, committed to transforming the lives of people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological disorders. from r&d to sales, our talented teams work together, revolutionizing treatment, continually improving products, understanding unmet needs, and connecting communities. we chase the miracles of science every single day, pursuing progress to make a real impact on millions of patients around the world.join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. in specialty care, you'll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs.about sanofiwe’re an r&d-driven, ai-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives.main responsibilitiesmanage communications activities across rare diseases, including both marketed and investigational products, with a focus on lysosomal storage disorders and support for select rare blood disorders as needed, including data and regulatory milestones, congresses, disease education and market-shaping activities.contribute to the development of comprehensive external communications plans that support rare diseases franchise priorities and align with global business objectives, and manage assigned activities through execution.manage the multichannel editorial calendar for global rare diseases franchise communications, coordinating inputs, approvals and timing across workstreams.support and oversee the development and activation of internal communications materials that support franchise priorities and promote consistent messaging across functions and geographies.partner with the in-house digital team on social media strategy, content development and internal approvals related to the rare diseases franchise, including product and investigational milestones.work with cross-functional partners to develop and execute thought leadership communications and platforms that support the reputation of the rare diseases franchise.manage day-to-day relationships with external communications agencies, providing clear direction, coordinating feedback and ensuring the timely delivery of high-quality materials.manage project timelines across multiple concurrent workstreams, anticipate risks, resolve routine issues and escalate significant concerns when appropriate.provide communications counsel and recommendations to internal stakeholders and cross-functional teams on messaging, positioning and reputational considerations, with guidance from the global head of rare diseases communications as needed.support communications planning for emerging issues by helping assess reputational risk, align messaging and prepare appropriate stakeholder responses.about youbasic qualifications:five years of communications experience in the healthcare industry, preferably within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology sector.demonstrated experience developing and executing strategic communications programs across multiple channels, with an understanding of key audiences, business objectives and the regulatory and reputational considerations shaping healthcare communications.proven ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment and manage defined workstreams while collaborating effectively in a cross-functional environment.strong project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects across teams and geographies, anticipate risks and adapt to shifting priorities.exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex scientific and business information into clear, audience-appropriate communications.strong relationship-building and influencing skills, with the confidence and judgment to work effectively with senior leaders and partners across functions overviewunder the supervision of the executive director, the communications and outreach manager for the wisconsin catholic conference (wcc) oversees communications initiatives that effectively describe and promote matters related to the beliefs, teachings, interests, and mission of the roman catholic church; provides decision makers with research and analysis; meets with diocesan staff; and educates parishioners. as permitted under wisconsin statutes s. 111.337(2), preference is for a practicing catholic in good standing with a strong commitment to the teachings and traditions of the roman catholic church.major responsibilitiesthe communications and outreach manager reports to the executive director and:1.     assists executive director and wcc staff with any project that may require those skills embodied by a communications professional. advises on effective communication techniques and messaging. drafts and disseminates wcc communications.2.     communicates the wcc’s positions on various issues and events to diocesan and secular media through news releases and other means, in consultation with the executive director. 3.     at the discretion of executive director, speaks for wcc on matters related to the teachings of the catholic church, including speaking to news media, presentations to parishes and other organizations, and is a public representative for the church’s teachings. at appropriate times, arranges wcc press conferences and assists in event planning and execution.4.     in coordination with wcc staff, manages wcc digital media, including website, social media, newsletter, and crm. develops and executes innovative programs to identify, contact, educate, and mobilize existing and potential supporters of wcc activities.  5.     develops wcc’s ideas and policy objectives into talking points, testimony, op-eds, letters to the editor, position papers, and more. in cooperation with wcc staff, prepares bi-weekly legislative updates, presentations, and other wcc publications.6.     monitors major wisconsin news media, social media, and other news sources to provide the executive director and wcc staff with recommendations of potential news items in need of response and prepares responses where appropriate.7.     convenes diocesan communication directors on an ongoing basis to discuss pertinent legislative matters and any other wcc activity that would impact upon diocesan staff. works closely with diocesan offices to provide assistance and foster inter-diocesan communication.8.     where appropriate, assists with representing the positions of the wcc to the legislature, legislative staff, and state agency personnel, providing decision makers with studied positions on social and moral issues, including public testimony before government committees and agencies.9.     demonstrates excellent verbal, written, analytical, and interpersonal skills.10. travels for professional development and to interact with catholics within wisconsin’s five dioceses. intermittent daytime and overnight travel are required. 11. performs other duties and tasks as directed by the executive director.basic qualificationscollege degree and/or experience, ideally related to one or more of the following: communications, journalism, marketing, public relations, political science, public policy, catholic theology, education, or lawknowledge of catholic social teachingwork with minimum supervision and high degree of independencewrite and speak clearly and persuasivelyproduce writing that adheres to wcc format and stylegive and receive critiques openly and generouslyinteract well with diverse individuals analyze problems and offer ethical and practical critiques, as well as policy solutionspreferred qualificationsadvanced degree and/or experience related to one of the following: communications, journalism, marketing, public relations, political science, public policy, catholic theology, education, or lawgeneral knowledge of catholic institutionsgraphic design and/or social media experienceknowledge of state and federal government, particularly the wisconsin legislaturespanish fluency (speaking, reading, and writing) is a pluslocationthe role will be on site in our office in madison, wi with normal working hours from 9:00am - 5:00pm monday through friday. salary & benefitsthe wisconsin catholic conference offers a robust benefits package including health insurance, dental insurance, parental leave, retirement plans, paid time off, and paid holidays including holy days of obligation. salary is dependent upon experience.how to applyinterested candidates should send a cover letter and resume to office@wisconsincatholic.org. priority application deadline is monday, november 30. references and a writing sample may also be requested from candidates selected to interview.

multilingual communication is available across all communications, including social media, flyers, translation materials, marketing materials, etc.  implement and maintain established communications experienced in constituent-facing communications and meeting the high expectations of residents seeking support from their local government.  detail-oriented and able to meet deadlines, with strong experience with microsoft office and google suite.  a track record of accomplishments centering on social equity and justice. termsboston residency requiredunion/salary plan/grade: care, supports for children with disabilities, broadened participation in stem, effective uses of digital learning, accessible college and career pathways, support for rural schools, and teacher role.experience in dissemination of research, technical assistance materials, and resources to various audiences including state policymakers and program administrators, private and nonprofit organizations, educators, school staff, students, families, and employers.ability to develop communication plans and products across channels and for different audiences.strong project management and executives.excellent written and oral communication skills.comfortable with frequent trips to customer locations within the arlington, va/washington dc area ability to travel outside the arlington, competitiveness and equity amongst internal employees in similar roles. positions may also qualify for sri's pay for outstanding performance program or the annual performance based compensation program. sri also has a competitive benefits package, to view details please go to https://www.sri.com/resources/benefits/. sri will accept applications until the position is filled.sri is an independent nonprofit research institute headquartered in menlo park, calif., with a rich history of supporting government and industry. we create and deliver world-changing solutions for a safer, trudon, the renowned luxury candlemaker from france, is seeking a pr & communications manager to join our u.s. team in new york.founded in 1643, trudon is the oldest continuously operating candlemaker in the world and was formerly the official supplier to the french royal court. known for exceptional craftsmanship and high-quality products, trudon produces artisanal candles, diffusers, fine fragrances, and body care that are cherished for their captivating scents and exquisite designs. we are committed to preserving the art of candle making while expanding our global presence.the pr & communications manager is responsible for developing and executing communications initiatives for trudon and carrière frères across the u.s. market. working closely with the paris marketing team and u.s. team, this role manages day-to-day press relations, develops influencer initiatives and facilitates brand events while identifying opportunities to strengthen the visibility and desirability of both brands within the luxury, fragrance, beauty and lifestyle landscape.the ideal candidate brings strong u.s. market knowledge, established media and industry relationships, and the ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.key responsibilities:communications planningdevelops and executes u.s. communications plans aligned with the global brand strategy established by paris headquarters and key u.s. business priorities.identifies relevant media, cultural and industry opportunities to increase brand visibility.adapts global communications initiatives to the u.s. market in collaboration with the paris marketing team and u.s. team.monitors industry trends and competitor activity to identify relevant opportunities.press relationsdevelops and executes u.s. press relations initiatives for trudon in alignment with the global communications priorities.builds and maintains relationships with editors, journalists and media contacts across luxury, design, fragrance, beauty and lifestyle.coordinates product launches, press releases, media outreach, interviews and product seeding.monitors media coverage and prepares regular reporting and market insights.influencer & creator relationsdevelops and executes influencer and creator initiatives aligned with trudon and carrière frères brand positioning and global priorities.cultivates relationships with influencers and creators on social media, including tiktok, instagram, and youtube.coordinates targeted gifting and seeding initiatives around product launches and key brand moments.manages partnerships from outreach through execution and follow-up; tracks activity and performance to identify future opportunities.develop an impactful affiliation strategy for carrière frères.events & brand activationsplans and coordinates press events, influencer activations, product launches and other brand experiences across off-site venues, the trudon showroom and u.s. retail locations.manages event logistics, guest lists, suppliers and budgets.partners with the broader team to ensure activations appropriately reflect each brand's identity and positioning.supports the identification of relevant local cultural and industry opportunities.cross-functional collaboration.partners with the u.s. sales and commercial retail teams on launches, events and other initiatives.works closely with the paris team to adapt global initiatives into u.s. market appropriate.shares relevant u.s. market trends, media insights and competitive observations.tracks u.s. communications-related expenditures and ensure activities remain within approved budgets.provides regular updates on press, influencer and event activity, results and opportunities for monthly results to achieve kpis.from time to time and at its absolute discretion, trudon may require you to perform any other reasonable duties which are commensurate with your job title in order to meet its business needs.what we are looking for:trudon and carrière frères are brands rooted in heritage, storytelling, craftsmanship, and culture. the ideal candidate is someone who is passionate about these topics and is able to work in a fast-paced entrepreneurial environment, while also enjoying building meaningful relationships with media, influencers and industry partners.they are equally comfortable contributing to communications planning and executing day-to-day activities with precision and attention to detail.5+ years of experience in public relations, communications or brand communications, either within an agency or in-house, with established relationships across relevant u.s. media and industry contacts.highly operational, proactive and organized, with excellent project management skills.strong understanding of the u.s. social media and creator landscape, particularly instagram, tiktok and youtube; experience working with content creators and developing social-first communications initiatives is a
