position summarythe senior graphics & packaging designer is a senior hands-on creative practitioner who personally conceives, designs, develops and delivers packaging and product graphics for key tomy international brands and npd programs. reporting to the vp npd & innovation, the role combines an active design workload with responsibility for raising creative standards and ensuring consistent, commercially effective execution across assigned projects.the senior personally owns complex and high-visibility briefs from first concept through production-ready artwork, including original layouts, visual systems, product graphics and design refinements. alongside this direct design output, the senior reviews colleagues' work, gives practical creative direction, coordinates priorities and coaches other designers. the vp retains overall creative vision, strategic direction and final escalation authority. the senior partners with brand, global npd, product integrity, legal/ip, operations, suppliers and marcoms, product engineering, final regulatory approval and manufacturing project management remain with their respective owners.key responsibilities1. hands-on packaging design & creative leadership• personally create original packaging concepts, visual directions, layouts, graphics, imagery briefs and polished design presentations for assigned npd and brand projects.• execute and refine artwork, typographic hierarchy, packaging architecture, product graphics and multi-sku design systems to a high creative and technical standard.• retain direct design ownership of high-priority and complex briefs from concept through prototypes, production artwork, proof review and final handoff; guide designers on other workstreams.• present and defend the lead's own design work using consumer, retail, brand and commercial rationale; review and strengthen the team's designs and escalate major choices where needed.• develop and deliver globally aligned packaging solutions that ensure brand consistency across international markets, while accommodating regional consumer needs, retailer requirements, local regulations and production efficiencies. 2. design team guidance, coaching & work priorities• balance a substantial personal design workload with day-to-day creative guidance; help prioritize briefs and flag capacity constraints so hands-on delivery remains achievable.• run practical design critiques, demonstrate solutions through sketches and artwork when helpful, and coach senior and developing designers through constructive feedback.• (future) build team capability through shared tools, best-practice examples, creative reviews and production knowledge; foster a collaborative, accountable culture.• flag capacity, capability or delivery risks early; support the creative director with resource planning and performance input as appropriate.3. consumer, brand & commercial design leadership• ensure packaging reinforces approved brand positioning, play benefits, product differentiation and price-value architecture across channels.• apply global brand and licensor guardrails consistently while enabling justified regional adaptation and effective localization.• challenge briefs and creative solutions using shopper insight, retail visibility, digital shelf effectiveness, cost and sustainability considerations.• align brand, marketing, sales and npd partners on clear packaging choices; recommend practical trade-offs that strengthen commercial outcomes.4. hands-on production craft, standards & risk• personally prepare and check production-ready artwork, dielines, print specifications, proofs, instructions, labels and product graphics on owned projects; set quality standards for the wider team.• work directly in design files with suppliers and production partners to solve color, finish, substrate, localization and artwork feasibility challenges.• partner with product integrity, legal/ip and operations to identify and resolve packaging risks before approvals or production commitments.• improve master artwork, digital asset management, templates and approval records to reduce rework, error rates and avoidable cost.5. cross-functional delivery & stakeholder leadership• deliver assigned design projects directly while coordinating the wider portfolio's briefs, milestones, reviews, approvals and dependencies with relevant partners.• act as the primary day-to-day creative interface for npd, brand, sales, regional teams, suppliers and marketing shared services on packaging programs.• lead packaging contributions to line reviews, customer presentations, range launches and trade shows, ensuring coherent and accurate outputs.• escalate significant scope, strategy, budget or creative conflicts to the department lead with clear options and recommended solutions.6. design systems, innovation & continuous improvement• personally develop reusable packaging design systems, master artwork and templates that maintain brand coherence and accelerate efficient sku extensions.• champion design experimentation, creative standards and trend awareness, converting relevant shopper and category learning into better design.• standardize review, briefing and handoff routines; measure errors, rework and design throughput and act on recurring issues.• encourage collaboration between packaging, product design and marketing while preserving functional ownership and decision boundaries.• drive innovation in packaging design, materials and formats, exploring creative solutions that enhance consumer appeal, improve sustainability and reduce environmental impact, while balancing production costs, commercial viability and scalability.qualificationsexperience• 8+ years of progressive packaging / graphic design experience, with evidence of recent, substantial hands-on creative and production work alongside leadership of complex consumer-product programs.• outstanding portfolio of personally designed packaging concepts and finished printed work, demonstrating original thinking, typography, range systems, retail impact and detailed production execution.• proven success leading multiple simultaneous briefs, prioritizing resources and influencing senior stakeholders in a matrix organization.• experience mentoring or supervising designers, conducting critiques, setting standards and improving delivery processes.• toy, games, collectibles, licensed consumer products, global brand systems or multi-market adaptation experience preferred.education & credentials• bachelor’s degree in graphic design, packaging design, visual communications or a related discipline preferred.• equivalent professional experience and a compelling design portfolio may substitute for formal degree requirements.skills & capabilities• expert hands-on concepting, graphic design, typography, packaging layouts, artwork preparation and creative visualization, alongside strong critique and design leadership skills.• expert in innovative structural packaging design and development, with strong hands-on skills in creating, prototyping and refining physical packaging mock-ups to validate functionality, presentation and commercial feasibility• expert, current working proficiency in adobe creative cloud and production files, print specifications, color, dielines, localization and artwork quality control.• portfolio and capacity planning, commercial judgement, cost-aware design, prioritization and risk management.• confident stakeholder presentations, negotiation, decision framing, constructive feedback and cross-functional influence.• team coaching, creative quality control and experience coordinating suppliers, agencies and global design partners.success measures• distinctive, high-quality packaging and product graphics personally designed and delivered for priority programs, with strong brand clarity and shelf impact.• reliable completion of the lead's own concept-to-production design assignments, alongside coordinated team milestones and balanced workloads.• lower artwork error, rework and production risk through clear quality gates and supplier-ready handoffs.• effective cross-region launches, licensor reviews and localization using scalable design systems.• evidence of stronger design output from colleagues through effective hands-on demonstration, constructive critique and coaching.• measurable improvements in team throughput, template reuse, process discipline and stakeholder confidence.

detail.desc: job title: communications manager at spirit of justice position type: full time location:  new york description: note: we encourage applicants to submit by dec 30th for priority consideration. while the application process will remain open on a rolling basis, candidates who apply by this date are most likely to be included in the first round of reviews by the search committee.about sojsoj is building a spiritual home for those who dare to dream of a more just and loving world — a beloved community where people from all backgrounds can deepen their inner lives, strengthen collective purpose, and transform themselves as they work to transform the world. soj was founded by acclaimed civil rights lawyer, legal scholar, and author michelle alexander, and is co-founded by nyle fort, a gifted minister, organizer, and scholar based at columbia university; the organization is fiscally sponsored by union theological seminary. at this pivotal moment in our nation and world, our movements cannot sustain themselves on strategy and resources alone; they require moral vision, courage, and deep reservoirs of love and resilience. soj aims to create the spiritually-grounded communal spaces our movements desperately need now – places where people can process fear and grief, cultivate courage and hope, develop moral clarity and sustain themselves for the long haul.  as a radically inclusive, non-dogmatic beloved community, soj is particularly committed to building community with the most vulnerable, including those who are queer and transgender people, from poor and working-class backgrounds, black and brown, people with disabilities, immigrants, as well as people who are currently and formerly incarcerated.  this is not a wellness program.  soj is co-creating a spiritual home rooted in a living tradition of revolutionary love that can be studied, practiced and carried forward, ultimately blossoming into a national network of beloved communities capable of defeating authoritarianism and rising to the challenges of our times.  what soj doessoj’s work rests on three core pillars that provide the home’s foundation:  1) storytelling, including a podcast hosted by michelle alexander that explores the spiritual lives of people committed to justice and liberation; 2) sanctuary, creating spaces for communities to engage in collective spiritual practice, fellowship and service, anchored by monthly and eventually weekly services, pods, movement chaplaincy and spiritual care, and a digital resource hub; and 3) seminary, including the development of a curriculum which anchors both political education and spiritual formation in the long lineage of revolutionary love. together, these pillars lay the foundation for the co-creation of beloved communities nationwide, a spiritual home shaped with care and intention by the very communities soj seeks to serve. mission of the rolereporting to the deputy director, and working closely with the executive director, deputy director and strategic communications consultant,  the communications manager will clearly and compellingly deliver spirit of justice’s message out into the world, shaping the voice, stories, and visuals that help people seeking deeper meaning and connection in their lives and justice work find their way to our spiritual home.areas of management & responsibilitymanage content production and community engagement for the soj substack newsletter, including:draft, edit, and publish newsletters, approximately two pieces per week.  draft, edit, and publish “notes” via the general soj account and on behalf of  soj leadership, as needed. actively monitor and engage the comment section of all newsletter and social media posts.  field inquiries and direct messages via the substack platform.   manage podcast distribution (two episodes per month) via soj-branded channels, including: youtube, spotify, apple music, etc.; actively monitor and engage in the comment sections of these platforms.  work closely with a third party consultant to develop and execute a marketing strategy for the podcast, including: analytic tools, seo strategies, and video-specific growth tactics.  manage the soj instagram (and eventually, other social media accounts), with a focus on publishing short video clips from podcast episodes.  make updates to the soj website as needed.  support the production of internal communications assets and documents as needed (memos, concept papers, business cards, thank you notes, flyers, etc).produce graphic and video assets for newsletters, events, and donor communications; manage subcontractors as needed.  participate in the development of a broader communications strategy for spirit of justice that will ensure the organization reaches diverse audiences across race/ethnicity, age, faith traditions, gender/sexuality, language, and ability.what success looks likethe soj podcast audience grows at a steady pace towards its goal of a 10,000 person listenership within the first six months of launching. the soj newsletter subscribership grows to 8,000 before the end of 2027.lively engagement is happening in the comment sections of the newsletter and social media accounts.  an annual content calendar is designed and executed.the soj website is well-maintained.  essential qualificationsgenuine values alignment with, or real interest in, spiritual, justice, and/or movement-adjacent work.impeccable attention to detail, highly reliable, and ability to juggle multiple projects at once.  strong, strategic writer and content creator with current internet-culture fluency and digital platform comfort.sound judgment and strong instincts for effective communications and engagement in online discourse. 3–4 years relevant experience, ideally including content management or campaign-adjacent digital roles.comfortable being edited and rewritten; strong execution and organizational skills.ability to manage subcontractors or freelancers, and to draft simple, clear statements.hands-on graphic design and short-form video editing skillsdirect experience maintaining a website and/or working knowledge of  website content management systemsunderstanding of digital analytics, seo and using data to inform content and growthexperience planning and managing a multi channel editorial/ content calendar experience creating content that is accessible and reaches diverse audiencescompensation & locationbudgeted salary: $90,000 soj’s salaries are designed to be as competitive as possible and are listed exactly as they are budgeted versus a range.  our intention is that this encourages alignment, transparency and pay equity. location: generally hybrid in the first year, though must be able to commute to new york city for various events and in-person meetings.  a future office location is planned at union theological seminary at 3041 broadway, new york, ny.

hi! 👋 i'm chris, head of product design at ashby.we're looking for a versatile, intrinsically motivated designer who is excited to contribute to rethinking how modern software is designed. at ashby, you'll be part designer, part product manager, part consultant, and part design system manager (or some combination of the 4!). we do design differently here, and if that excites you, read on.our unique approach is working - we're growing >100% year-over-year and have notable customers like notion, linear, shopify, and snowflake. our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in arr, very low churn, and many years of runway. we're backed by amazing investors like y combinator, elad gil, lachy groom, and many more! we’ll share more details once we meet.how we workin my previous roles, product teams always consisted of a product manager, a designer, and ~4-5 engineers. this may sound familiar to you! the product manager briefs the designer who then designs. after designing, mocks are handed to the engineers.we take a more principled approach here at ashby. if you've been designing software enough, you'll realize in actuality, design is required in varying degrees on each project. sometimes in the past, i'd be asked to design yet another settings page, when really all that was needed was an engineer to reuse existing components and just follow some documentation i had written. other times, i felt i should effectively be the product manager and own a project from beginning to end. in these latter cases, it made sense that i was even the one providing project updates and managing resources rather than constantly being pinged by a separate product manager.this principled approach is now what we do here, and it is part of what has allowed ashby to take down incumbents in multiple verticals all at once. we don't settle for the status quo—we actively resist reversion to the mean.currently, i report to benji, the co-founder & ceo. both abhik and benji (our founders) care deeply about design, which at first glance may seem counterintuitive given the number of full-time designers that we employ. the belief is not that design is unimportant, but rather that it should be owned by the product team collectively, not solely by a group of full-time designers who happen to have the job title.the design department’s job at ashby is not to make every single design decision but to equip our entire product team to make better decisions themselves, as well as edit decisions that pms/engineers choose to make. that, while tackling the biggest design challenges ourselves.separate from design, you may also be excited by the fact that we maintain a near seed-stage-like culture with fuzzy lines between functional roles, as much autonomy as you can handle, and a focus on ic-work with an almost-no-meeting culture. while you get the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup, you also get the agency and no-nonsense, no-red-tape culture of a seed-stage startup.what we’re buildingtalent teams aspire to build a hiring process that identifies great candidates, moves them quickly through the interview process, and provides an excellent experience for the candidate. to accomplish this, recruiters perform thousands of daily tasks to coordinate and relay information between candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers. teams struggle to keep up!scheduling a final round is an excellent example of our customers' challenges. a recruiter needs to collect availability from the candidate, identify potential interviewers, perform “calendar tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and perform any last-minute adjustments as availability changes. they must perform this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others.ashby provides and source content that marketing builds from: who the product is for, why it wins, and what story deserves telling.launch programs are planned and run by the corporate marketing program managers, and marketing messages are crafted within corporate marketing. you are the product-side counterpart both depend on: the upstream source, and the standard-setter for what product content should achieve as the company grows.what you will ownproduct definition. you sit with product line managers and define, for each priority product, the business opportunity: target applications and markets, the source content, and the product line's understanding of what resonates.cross-functional partnership. you are the connective role between the product lines and the corporate marketing teams that plan corporate marketing launch programs.product line managers treat content as leverage and come to you early, not after the launch date is set.performance readouts from corporate marketing visibly sharpen the product story and the next launch's source content.corporate marketing teams consider you their best briefing partner: clear inputs, realistic timelines, shared credit.what you bring8+ years in b2b marketing with depth in product marketing or content strategy for technical products. semiconductors, electronic components, or an adjacent engineering-driven industry is a strong plus.a track record of building content frameworks and standards: you have created something repeatable that outlived your involvement.fluency with performance data: you read analytics, draw conclusions, and hold your own with engineers and product line managers: technical curiosity, fast learning, and respect for accuracy.who you will work withyou will work daily with product line managers and applications engineers, and partner closely with the corporate marketing organization: the brand and creative team, technical content and documentation, digital marketing, and events. you report into about blinkrx:blinkrx is rebuilding how americans access life-changing medicines. today, only one in five prescriptions for new branded therapies are ever filled. the problem isn't the medicine. it's insurance barriers, affordability challenges, fragmented pharmacy experiences, and inadequate support that keep patients from starting and staying on treatment. our mission is to change that.we built rxos, the first ai-powered prescription operating system. rxos connects the largest network of doctors, patients, pharmacies, payers, and pharmaceutical manufacturers, intelligently orchestrating every step to guarantee a seamless prescription journey for every script.our teams solve complex, high-stakes problems at the intersection of artificial intelligence, healthcare operations, logistics, payments, and regulation. the impact is transformative: blinkrx more than doubles the rate at which patients take their medications and lowers their out-of-pocket expenses by hundreds of dollars every month.blinkrx created and leads a rapidly growing $80+ billion category, with exceptional momentum:built for scale: over the past decade, we have invested nearly $1 billion in building the technology and operational platform required to serve patients at scale.proven growth and economics: we have grown 100% annually for the past five years, are profitable, and support more than 60 pharmaceutical brands.trusted with category-defining programs: our technology powers a leading pharmaceutical manufacturer’s direct-to-patient platform for its glp-1 portfolio, providing the infrastructure to expand patient access as demand for these therapies grows.we are a dynamic team of technologists and industry experts seeking to build a generational company that delivers a genuine step change in american health.  blinkrx is looking for a creative operations manager to be the operational backbone of the creative team. our small but mighty in-house team are all makers at heart and care deeply about the quality of our work. we bring relentless focus, fast execution, and a passion for craftsmanship to everything we make.we are responsible for elevating blinkrx's brand and story and focused on creating high-impact, multi-channel marketing content, creative, and brand evolution. in this role, you’ll run how work gets requested, scoped, prioritized, staffed, reviewed, approved, delivered and archived. this applies to both the in-house team and the agencies and contractors we use. creative leaders should spend their time on creative decisions, not on chasing status, version confusion or unclear briefs.we require experience on both sides of the table. you’ve worked at an agency or studio, where you scoped, estimated, and managed client expectations. you’ve also worked at an in-house team, where you served internal stakeholders, handled competing priorities, and built trust over time. we want someone who can apply agency rigor inside an in-house team.key responsibilitiesown intake, scoping and prioritization: run the front door for creative requests with standard briefs, triage and readiness criteria. weigh competing demands against business priorities, say no or “not yet” constructively, and escalate trade-offs to creative leadership with clear data.plan capacity and resources: build capacity and utilization models across designers, motion, content, video, freelancers and agencies. forecast around launches, partner onboarding and events, and recommend when to hire, use freelancers or bring in an agency.manage agencies and vendors: own the agency and freelancer roster, including sows, estimates, onboarding, briefing standards and performance reviews. own the creative tech stack and drive adoption.design workflows, governance, and reviews: document and improve workflows, sops and approval routing, with review paths matched to each asset’s risk and format. partner with legal, compliance and partner teams so work is review-ready on first submission, and bring compliance input upstream to the concept stage.run rebrand and brand rollout operations: own the project and operational side of our branding, from managing the agency partner to rolling the new brand out to the company. make sure teams have the guidelines, assets, and templates they need and that the brand is applied consistently.enable the wider company: create self-serve resources and templates so sales, product and marketing can produce on-brand work without queuing for the design team. run regular rhythms (weekly planning, retros, quarterly roadmap reviews) and support creative budget tracking. requirements6+ years in creative or marketing operations, pmo, resource management or agency operations. meaningful time at both an agency/studio and an in-house creative or brand team, with specific examples of what you learned in each.demonstrated ownership of intake, resourcing, workflow design and reporting for a creative team, not just project coordination.experience with scopes, estimates, budgets and vendor or freelancer management.experience managing the project and operational side of a rebrand and rolling it out throughout the organization.fluency in work-management and proofing tools.strong analytical skills. you build the dashboard and then act on it.credibility with creatives and with executives. you push back with data and keep stakeholders calm under deadline pressure.experience in healthcare, pharma, fintech or another regulated industry with formal review or approval processes preferred. why join us:it is rare to have a company that both deeply impacts its customers and is able to provide its services across a massive population.  at blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances. we are also the fastest growing healthcare company in the country and are driving that impact across millions of new patients every year.  our business model not only helps people, but drives economics that allow us to build a generational company. we are a relentlessly learning, constantly curious, and aggressively collaborative cross-functional team dedicated to inventing new ways to improve the lives of our customers.we are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity of all kinds. we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national detail.desc: about ussynthesis is a creative data consultancywe help future-proof businesses by making sense of the world’s data.we partner with industry leaders like netflix, nike, pepsico and airbnb to define their audiences and how their needs will evolve over the short and long term.we do this through our unique synthesis of deep human understanding and data science. our team brings together diverse specialists from computer science, digital anthropology and engineering, digital forensics, scriptwriting and the humanities.why synthesis?since our launch in 2017, we’ve been reimagining the world of marketing and strategy. we build deep global partnerships, especially in entertainment, travel, f&b, and beauty categories. we answer complex, future-facing questions by detecting early signals of change and surfacing opportunities to win with new audiences. our specialized solutions are rooted in culture and tested through data science, giving our partners the confidence to act.our culture and futures teams work hand in hand. culture tells us what people value today and why; futures tells us where that is heading and what it means for the business. together they help brands build strong foundations, define distinctive positioning territories, identify innovation opportunities and plan for the next 5-10 years.example challenges we’ve worked on recently include:helping a world cup sponsor identify the cultural narratives with greatest potential for its ads and activationsunderstanding the impact of macro forces on the future of snackingexploring the changing role of family in modern america to shape culturally resonant, human-centered positioning for a technology platformmodelling future consumption demand to identify emerging categories to invest inabout the roleamericas: north america (usa, canada) & latamas a senior strategist, you'll be a builder, working closely with the team to deepen relationships with our americas-based partners. we’ve had strong growth in our first couple of years in nyc, and want to build on this momentum. you’ll regularly work with our singapore and london teams, sharing projects, thinking, frameworks, and tech, helping you shape a perspective most strategists never get. this role sits across our culture and futures practices. you will read the cultural shifts shaping consumers today and project where they will take people, categories and brands over the next 5-10 years. some projects will lean on one discipline more than the other; some will need both.day-to-day, the role will be anchored in consulting projects, growing our partnerships and building team culture. you will have a hand in boldly stretching our technical and creative outputs to ensure that synthesis thinking, workflows, and technology are ahead of the curve, differentiated from the competition, and delivering strong results for the sharpest insights and marketing professionals in the world.your core focusfluency in what's changing, across time horizons. you understand the macro forces reshaping the world and how they show up as shifts in culture, consumer expectations, category dynamics, and brand behavior. you are comfortable working across all three horizons: what is happening now (h1), what is emerging over the next few years (h2), and the longer-term futures further out (h3). you can move between them from one project to the next, or within the same piece of work, and you tell human stories backed by data.connecting the now and the next. you can trace a cultural signal from its early edges to its commercial consequences, and tell a client which shifts will fade, which will last, and what to do about each.able to turn data complexity into a clear point of view. you're comfortable working with complex data sets. you can connect seemingly disparate signals and turn them into a clear point of view that helps clients make confident decisions about where to play and how to win.a trusted strategic partner, not a project manager. you immerse yourself in each client's business, ambitions, and competitive reality. this enables you to deliver outcomes that go beyond being culturally and future relevant to being commercially impactful.a confident facilitator and presenter. you can lead senior stakeholders through complex conversations with clarity and conviction. you are comfortable commanding a room, adapting in real time, and bringing diverse perspectives together to drive meaningful outcomes.startup mentality and a love of business development. you get a thrill from winning projects, writing proposals, pitching, and chasing down new leads to grow clients across the business.making people around you better. you're generous with what you know and support others in their development so our overall work is continuously getting sharper.about working herewe are a diverse team, we value creativity, ‘plussing’ and teamwork. to help create this environment, we offer a flexible, supportive work environment. this includes the following benefits:the salary range for this position is us$100,000-us$150,000.profit-sharing bonus scheme.flexible working hours with 3 days in the office.20 days paid vacation per annum + public holidays + whole company wellness week between christmas and new year.12 weeks paid maternity leave or 4 weeks paid paternity leave.private healthcare and wellness allowance.the office. we have a private space in a cozy co-working space right beside mccarren park in greenpoint, brooklyn.about youyou’ll have 5+ years of experience in research, innovation, trends and foresight, strategy and planning, management consultancy, or related roles.you will have worked on complex projects for major consumer brands, ideally in the f&b, entertainment, travel or beauty spaces. this includes experience in analyzing quant, qual and other research methodologies.you have delivered both culture and futures work, or you have gone deep in one and show strong curiosity about, and some evidence of, the other.you are a great storyteller with a nose for insights and stretchy, fresh and memorable thinking on familiar topics.you are biased towards high-quality thinking and meticulous output. you know that short, actionable outputs that drive decisions are valuable to senior stakeholders. you are allergic to 200-slide decks.you use ai every day: to find patterns you’d otherwise miss, push your thinking further and take repetitive work off your plate. you never let it replace your judgment.you are curious about people and comfortable with data. you appreciate the advantage that human understanding at scale can bring to businesses.
